title: What changed
dek: Every search this archive has run and every claim it has taken back, newest first.
lead:
Most family archives publish only what they found. This one publishes **what it looked for, what it found, what it did not find, and what it got wrong** — in one feed, in the order it happened.

A search that returned nothing is kept because **an absence from a named source is a finding**, and because the next person should not have to repeat it. A correction is kept because an archive that only shows its successes is not telling you how reliable it is.

rows.text: **A third wife named in the parents' generation.** 17 July 1832, house 325: **Domenico De Franceschi**, forty-six and a widower, «figlio delli furono giugali **Pietro De Franceschi e Martina Civico q.m Domenico**, Vedovo della q.m **Veniera De Rocchi fu Onorato**», marries a widow. Because both parties are widowed the clerk writes every name out, and it yields a couple this archive did not have. **Martina Civico** joins Michiela Zambaletta and Domenica Manzin as the third named wife of that generation. Whether her husband Pietro is the same man as the Pietro q.m Domenico who married Domenica Manzin is left **open** — this parish has produced four Pietros and two Cristoforos, and only a patronymic settles it. Don Stefano witnesses a **nineteenth** time, 16 November 1832.

rows.what: Late 1832 into 1833
rows.text: **A second son, and a correction.** 1 December 1832, house 282: «**Domenico figlio di Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria e della q.m Veniera Francin q.m Domenico**», aged 29 — the same parents as the 1821 bridegroom, so a **younger brother of Gio: Maria**, born about 1803. And on **26 January 1833** the priest's signature reads «**D.n Stefano De Franceschi, De Parochi lic., li congiunse e benedisse nella Chiesa Parrocchiale**» — **he married them himself**, which retires this archive's repeated claim that he was never the officiant. The claim was true of 1819–1832 and was stated as though it covered a book that was still sixty openings from being read. What survives is better: he acts «De Parochi lic.», by the parson's licence, the same formula as the 1816 baptism.

rows.what: February 1833
rows.text: **Giuseppe De Franceschi's death bracketed.** The weaver is «Cristoforo De Franceschi ***di*** Giuseppe» in March 1818 and November 1828, and «***fu*** Giuseppe» on 12 February 1833 — so the father of the priest, the ploughman and the weaver **died between November 1828 and February 1833**. Also **Don Stefano officiates a second time**, in the church of the **B. V. del Carmine**, and **Pietro De Franceschi fu Pietro** witnesses a third time. And a reading withdrawn the day after publishing it: «**De Par. lic.**» is the register's **standard formula for any deputising priest** — the next entry uses it of Don Pietro Bradamante — not the personal arrangement this archive took it for. Vodnjan is running marriages through at least four churches: the parish church, San Martino, the B. V. del Carmine and the B. V. della Trovesa.

rows.what: 1833: the brothers' own household
rows.text: **The household of the priest, the ploughman and the weaver opens.** 27 July 1833, house 324: «**Maria Francesca, figlia del fu Giuseppe De Franceschi q.m Pietro e di Lucia Tromba q.m Cristoforo**», marrying at twenty-eight. That gives Giuseppe **a father (Pietro)**, **a wife (Lucia Tromba)** and **a fourth child** — and confirms his death inside the bracket his sons' patronymics had already set, after November 1828 and before February 1833. **The mother is a Tromba**: the surname of **Giovanni Tromba S.T.D., the parroco who signs every page** and who licensed her son Don Stefano to baptise in 1816 and to marry couples in 1833. One of the two witnesses is Andrea Tromba, Possidente Civile. A ploughman's and a weaver's family produced a priest of the chapter, and their mother came from the family that held the parish. *(the kinship is inf, on a shared surname in a small town)*

rows.what: Opening the death register
rows.text: **The third book on the film, and it is not indexed either.** Deaths 1815–1833 run from about image 471 to 575 — thirteen entries a page, six images to the year, in a Latin ruling with a cause-of-death column. A query for De Franceschi deaths 1826–1836 across the whole of Croatia returns **eight dated records and none from this parish**. First entry read: **11 March 1829, house 325, «Maria, figlia di Stefano De Franceschi e di Bonetta Vellico q.m Antonio»** — a child of one of the eight households reconstructed from the baptism index, which now has a burial and a house number. Images 546–548 read; the target is **Giuseppe De Franceschi**, bracketed by his sons' patronymics to between November 1828 and February 1833.

rows.what: 1829, and two households given their dead
rows.text: **Two of the eight reconstructed households now have a burial, a house number and — in one case — a generation above them.** 11 March 1829, house 325: «Maria, figlia di **Stefano De Franceschi e di Bonetta Vellico q.m Antonio**». 23 July 1829, house 48: «Pietro, figlio di **Dom.co De Franceschi *q.m Pietro* e di Zacchera Cerlon di Franc.o**» — which names Domenico's own dead father, a **Pietro**, where the baptism index had only a bare pair of names. Also caught and fixed: the reader's crops were being **clipped to the viewport, losing the bottom fifth of every page**, silently. Images scanned before the fix are being re-scanned.

rows.what: Automated reading, stopped
rows.src: FamilySearch — both the persona API and the Deep Zoom image service
rows.text:
**403 — «This request was blocked by our security service.»** After two days of reading register images tile by tile, FamilySearch's bot protection has blocked this session: the persona search endpoint and the `deepzoomcloud` image service both now return a 403 with a NOINDEX/NOFOLLOW block page rather than data.

**No attempt has been made or will be made to get around it.** This archive does not bypass bot checks or CAPTCHAs, and a block is a legitimate answer from a service that has given it a very great deal already — five generations at Vodnjan came off these films in two days.

**What this stops, for now:** the rest of the Vodnjan marriage register (images 217–470), the death registers (546–575 on film 894 and all of 895), the Vodnjan baptism re-read, Svetvinčenat's marriage register, and the Rijeka and Bakar films. Those six items are paused, not abandoned.

**What it does not stop:** everything already read and published, and the work that does not touch FamilySearch — the itineraries, the portraits, the archive letters, and the reconciliation of David's own GEDCOM when it arrives.

rows.what: Giuseppe De Franceschi, found
rows.text: **The bracket closes exactly.** This archive had no date for Giuseppe De Franceschi — only a range derived from how his sons were written, «*di* Giuseppe» in November 1828 and «*fu* Giuseppe» in February 1833. The death register gives **14 February 1830**: «**Giuseppe De Franceschi q.m Pietro era ammogliato con Lucia Tromba fu Cristoforo**», **house 324**, **aged 72** — so born about **1758** — of an **organic defect of the chest**, and, in the sacraments column, «**senza assistenza spirituale per morte improvvisa**»: **suddenly, with no priest**. His own son was a priest of that parish. **And five months later, 13 July 1830, house 501: «Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro era Moglie di Alviso Birattan q.m Sabà», aged 70**, of dropsy — the woman whose three daughters married out in 1821, 1824 and 1825. **Both «q.m Pietro», born about 1758 and 1760, dead five months apart**: almost certainly brother and sister, which joins the two households and puts a Pietro born around 1730 behind both.

rows.what: House 325 gets its family
rows.text: **11 September 1830, house 325: «Bonetta Vellico q.m Antonio, Moglie di Stefano De Franceschi *di* Domenico *q.m* Pietro»**, aged 57 — born about 1773 — of pulmonary consumption, eighteen months after her daughter died in the same house. The two different words matter: ***di*** Domenico means **his father was alive**; ***q.m*** Pietro means his grandfather was not. A third Vodnjan line stands — **Pietro → Domenico → Stefano** — and it gives that household three generations where the baptism index gave none. It also makes **house 325 theirs**, which sharpens the question raised two days ago: the same number stands against Domenico De Franceschi, 46, son of a Pietro and Martina Civico, remarrying there in 1832. The connection is now **likely**; which connection it is stays **open**, because on the stated ages that Domenico is too young to be Stefano's father.

rows.what: Deaths, late 1830 – Feb 1833
rows.text: **The tile server refused.** `image.xml` still answered 200, but every image tile came back **403** from the Incapsula security service, at every zoom level, on the first request of the session — no CAPTCHA offered, no rate warning, nothing to wait out. **No attempt was made to get round it.** The reading stops here until the block lifts. The targets it was going to answer — **Luigetta De Franceschi**, dead by November 1831; **Martina Civico** and **Veniera De Rocchi**, both dead by 1832 — stay open on What we cannot close.

rows.what: Vodnjan households, mined from the catch instead of the film
rows.text:
With the film shut, the **1,508-row catch harvested the day before** was read for parent-pairs instead. It gave **four households the archive did not have** — *Sebastiano Giachin × Domenica De Franceschi* (1817–1832), *Giuseppe Forlani × Lucia Michiela De Franceschi* (1848–1857), *Stefano De Franceschi × Maria Forlanichio* (1858–1860) and *Domenico De Franceschi × Mattea Delcarro* (1858–1865) — plus **two children** for households already standing: **Teresa Domenica**, 1820, to Pietro and Maria Malusà, and **Lucia**, 25 July 1826, to Gio Maria and Lucia Bonassin.

It also gave a **warning about itself**. A ninth apparent household, *Giovanni Moscarda × Maria Defranceschi*, dissolved on inspection: **Antonio 1835 and Antonio 1836, Stefano 1844 and Stefano 1844, Epifanio and Giovanni Epifano both June 1849** are the same children indexed twice, in Latin and in Italian. Nothing was added from it. That is the Register's own caveat — *an entry is not a person* — proving itself within a day of being published.

rows.what: December 1830 – January 1831
rows.text:
**Entry 151, 15 December 1830, house 456.** «Pietro figlio di Pietro De Franceschi **q.m Pietro** e di Maddalena Francin **di Giovanni** giugali», aged **11**, of **scarlatina**, and in the sacraments column «**senza assistenza spirituale per la malattia repentina**».

He is a **new eldest child** for a household this archive already had — three years older than its earliest baptism — so **that marriage was made by 1818**, not 1822. His father's father was dead by 1830; his mother's father was alive. The house is **456**, a third Vodnjan house number after 324 and 325.

**Entry 4, 6 January 1831, house 24.** «Domenica figlia di Andrea Palin q.m Pio. e **della fu Michiela De Franceschi fu Pietro** giugali» — a **sixth** woman who left the surname, dead before 1831, recoverable only because her daughter died young enough to need her named.

**Two rejected.** Entry 157 reads «Nicolò Sussani **q.m Francesco**» and entry 16 «Antonia Palin **di Francesco**». Both are patronymics. At low zoom both looked like the surname; neither is.

rows.what: Scarlatina, December 1830
rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 560, entries 149–155
rows.text: Five of seven consecutive entries — **150, 151, 152, 153, 155** — give the cause as «**Scarlatina**», and the dead are aged **7, 11, 6, 6** and a child. **Scarlet fever went through Vodnjan in December 1830**, and the eleven-year-old Pietro De Franceschi died in it. The register writes the age as «d'an. 11» in a column headed *Aetas*; the two entries on either side of him are other people's children of six and seven.

rows.what: A slip of paper left in the book
rows.text:
Image 561 is a **re-shoot of the same opening as 560**, with a loose slip laid across the left page — so the December 1830 entries are hidden and the slip is filmed instead.

**Recto:** «**Cercare ne' libri de' morti — Maria Celin fu moglie del fu Marco Silla, morto da anni 25, 26 c.a**» — someone's instruction to *search the books of the dead*.

**Verso, upside down:** a draft entry — «**165 · Dom.ca Gasparro fu Dom.co e Cat.a Baldarin № 505, morta li 23 ottobre 1843, da male di petto**», then two names, «**Giorgio Cossich e Fran.co Maravo**».

Neither side concerns this family. It is kept because of what it is: **parish office scrap from 1843, lying in an 1831 opening, photographed because nobody moved it** — and on one side of it, somebody else's unfinished search.

rows.what: February 1831, first half
rows.text: Twelve entries, 1–11 February 1831, read in full: Portolato, Manzin, Toffetti, Vidich, Rotta, Muscovich, Del Carro, Ciritico, Cattarin, Gasparo Toffetti. **No De Franceschi.** The second half of the page was not reached — the security service blocked the film mid-page.

rows.what: February 1831 onward
rows.src: Vodnjan, Liber Defunctorum — DGS 005497894, image 562 onward
rows.text: **Blocked mid-page.** After roughly four hundred tile requests the Incapsula service began returning **403 on `image.xml` itself**, which had answered 200 all session. The reading stopped there. No pacing was tried, no route was looked for, no request was repeated. The film is open at **image 562, second half**, and that is where it resumes.

rows.what: Every household in the catch, not just Vodnjan's
rows.text:
With the film blocked, the whole catch was mined for parent-pairs rather than only its Istrian rows. It gave **48 households the archive did not have**, holding **151 children** — among them *Veneranda Defranceschi × Antonius Subiotto* (eight children, 1858–1874), *Pascha Defranceschi × Angelus Ferrarese* (seven, 1849–1864), *Francesco Franceschi × Maria De Caralipeo* at **Almissa in Dalmatia** (seven, 1856–1873), and *Josephi Defranceschi × Mariæ Defranceschi* at **Ližnjan** (five, 1872–1888).

Every one is filed **`index`, not `read`** — the pattern is real, the spellings are the indexer's, and no page has been seen. **34 are in Istria, 11 in Dalmatia, 10 in the Kvarner and 43 could not be placed at all.**

**Three pairs are flagged as possibly one household each** — *Bellinich* twice, *Zanghirella* twice, *Lazar* twice — where the surnames match once the spellings are set aside and the years all but touch. They are **kept apart**, because merging two households on a surname is how one family becomes a fiction.

The merge itself had to be built twice. The first pass counted **100** pairs, most of them Latin genitives of each other — *Valentini* and *Valentino*, *Ursulæ* and *Orsola*, *Josephi* and *Giuseppe* — and *Francetich* rows that are not this family at all. Normalising the genitives, collapsing doubled letters and requiring a **De Franceschi** parent brought it to 48.

rows.what: 1948: an attempt to leave the country
rows.text:
Asked what «went» meant, David answered: **«They went to leave the country in 1948.»**

That converts a contradiction into a **window**. Their son was born at Senj on **17 December 1951**, so they were back on the coast by about **March 1951**; Ivan died at Senj in 1995. **They left in 1948, were home inside about two and a half years, and never got out** — Hedviga reached Johannesburg only much later, and Ivan never did.

The route is not a mystery either. The family already had a household in **Pfullingen, in the French occupation zone**: Ivan had worked at Reutlingen from 21 October 1941, his father was on the 1947 Pfullingen list of foreigners, and his brothers **Zdravko and Anton** went out to Australia from there in **1949** — Anton's card stamped «Emigré Australie le 8.3.49». **Ivan and Hedviga were a year behind them at a door that was closing**, the IRO shutting its books at the end of February 1952.

**A failed exit leaves no Yugoslav paper.** The Arolsen request has been rewritten accordingly and is now the highest-value errand this project holds.

rows.what: The people known only from the tree
rows.text:
All **101** people this archive held as a name and nothing else were pulled from the tree, one panel at a time, from David's own logged-in session. **No errors, and one flat result: the tree has no years for them either.** Exactly **one** of the hundred and one carries a date range, and it is not a date this archive accepts — see below.

What the tree did give was **place**. **48 of them are now placed**, and the places are the deep end of the story: **Mione in the Val Degano eight times**, **Paluzza five**, **Naunina**, **Pasian di Prato** — Carnia, where the surname is supposed to come from. Then a Trentino cluster the archive barely knew it had — **Fiera di Primiero, Telve, Strigno, Grigno, Sacco** — and Istrian parishes at **Kaštelir (five), Poreč, Pula, Pomer, Plomin, Pazin, Gologorica, Ližnjan**. Two are in **South America**: San Lorenzo in Santa Fe, and Colonia in Uruguay.

**15 people are now filed to Carnia, 8 to Trentino, 2 abroad** — lines they could not be given while they had no place. Roster people with no place at all: **209 → 161**. Parishes known to this archive: **31 → 54**.

rows.what: Piero della Francesca is in the family tree
rows.text:
The one dated person among the hundred and one is «**Piero di Benedetto «Piero della Francesca» Defranceschi, 1415–1492, Sansepolcro**» — the painter — together with his father **Benedetto Defranceschi** and his mother **Romana di Perino**.

The surname is not the error. Piero's father genuinely was a *de' Franceschi* of Sansepolcro; that much is ordinary art history. **The error, if it is one, is the join** — nothing whatever connects a Tuscan tanner's family to the Carnian and Istrian Defranceschi except the word itself.

All three are kept in the roster, marked **notable**, filed under *other*, and each carries the same sentence: *the connection to this family is not accepted*. **A Tuscan graft on a Friulian surname is exactly the kind of join this archive exists to catch** — and it is the third time this project has had to say so, after Francesco de' Franceschi the Venetian printer and Francesco de' Franceschi the painter.

rows.what: Ivan Defranceski, Hedviga Blažević, Uršula Kovačina, Anton Rudolf — 1948–1951
rows.text:
**Not attempted: the service is down.** `collections.arolsen-archives.org` resolves to 62.90.197.110 and **times out**, while the main Arolsen site answers normally — so the online archive, not the organisation, is unavailable. David confirms it is dead from his side too, so it is not a block on this machine.

**It stays on the list.** The four searches are *Defranceski*, *Defranceschi*, *Blazevic Hedviga*, *Kovacina Ursula*, and the window that matters is **1948–1951** — the only place the failed exit can have left a trace, since a departure that was reversed leaves nothing in any Croatian register. A record of **Anton Rudolf after 1943** would separately settle whether Uršula was a widow or a wife when the man called **Car** appears.

The written enquiry to Bad Arolsen is drafted and waiting, and is deliberately **not** being sent first: their own advice is to search the online archive before joining a queue they warn may run to thirteen months.

rows.what: Whether the Croatian church books are machine-readable yet
rows.text:
**A maybe, recorded so it is not lost.** FamilySearch has been extending an AI handwriting-recognition search that makes the **text inside register images** searchable rather than only the catalogue around them. **Whether the Croatian church books are in it is not known** — it has not been tested, and FamilySearch is refusing this session at the time of writing.

It matters more than anything else on the list. Reading Vodnjan's death register 1815–1833 by eye is about **105 images and four and a half thousand entries**; if the text is already searchable, that work is a query instead of a campaign. **Test this before committing to any exhaustive read**, because a positive answer makes the plan obsolete and a negative one costs a single request.

If it is not available: the fallback is **handwritten-text recognition trained on this clerk's hand** — twenty pages transcribed by hand to train on, then the rest by machine. That costs money and setup and is **David's decision, not this archive's**.

rows.what: «Corsica — not ours»
rows.text: **This archive said** The lines page filed Corsica under «**not ours**». **What is true** **Nobody had checked.** Not one search had ever been run in a French archive for this surname, in any commune. «Not ours» was a **guess wearing the clothes of a finding** — the same error as a false join, made in the opposite direction. **How it happened** Replaced with a stated position and its reasoning on a page of its own: a **parallel, not a branch**, expected to be unrelated and **not yet tested**. **Dismissing a line without looking is exactly as unevidenced as claiming one.**

rows.what: «Nine parishes» on the Archive page
rows.text:
**This archive said** «**1,151 registers catalogued across nine parishes**» — the count of books was computed from the data, the count of parishes was typed by hand.

**What is true** There are **fourteen**: Barban, Cerovlje, Gologorica, Gračišće, Ližnjan, Motovun, Pazin, Pićan, Poreč, Svetvinčenat, Umag, Vižinada, Vodnjan and Čepić.

**How it happened** Now computed from the same data as the number beside it. **Any figure a page states should be derived, not typed** — a hand-typed number is right on the day it is written and wrong from then on.

rows.what: What the Archive's 1,151 actually counts
rows.text:
**This archive said** Nothing false — but the page led with **1,151** and let a reader assume it was a measure of the project's reach. Set beside a sister site's **10,536 records naming 4,779 people**, it invited exactly the wrong comparison.

**What is true** **1,151 counts books, not people.** It is the Pazin inventory of parish registers that exist. This archive has opened a book in **7 of the 14 parishes**, and most of the **997 digitised** volumes have never been looked at. The comparable people-counts are **1,136** on Everyone and **1,508** on The Register.

**How it happened** The page now says so in its own words, and says why the sister project's number is larger: it **read a town's death registers act by act** rather than searching an index for one surname. **1,151 is not an achievement. It is the size of the job.**

rows.what: Piero della Francesca in the family tree
rows.text:
**This archive said** Nothing on this site — the claim is in **the family's own MyHeritage tree**, which places the painter **Piero della Francesca (1415–1492)** of Sansepolcro in this family, with his father Benedetto and mother Romana di Perino.

**What is true** Piero's father genuinely was a **de' Franceschi** of Sansepolcro, so the surname is real. **The connection to the Carnian and Istrian family is not.** Nothing documents it, and nothing here claims it.

**How it happened** Recorded rather than deleted, because the tree is a source this archive reads and it is better to name a doubtful join than to leave it unmentioned. All three are marked so on their own pages. **This is the third famous namesake the project has had to refuse** — after the Venetian printer and the Venetian painter — and the pattern is always the same: a well-known man of the name, and no join but the name.

rows.what: Hedviga Blažević has two birthdays
rows.text: **This archive said** Two pages give her birth as **8 March 1926**. A third page quotes the certified extract of the Senj birth register, attached to her son's 1951 entry, which gives **3 August 1926**. **What is true** **Both have stood on this site at once and nobody noticed.** Written as numbers they are **8/3/1926** and **3/8/1926** — a day and a month exchanged, almost certainly where a European date met an English-speaking translator. This archive does not know which is right. **How it happened** **Neither has been quietly deleted.** Both now stand, marked as in conflict, and the Senj birth register for 1926 is an errand. The lesson is one this project keeps relearning: **a date that appears twice in an archive should be diffed, not trusted twice.**

rows.what: Anton Rudolf, dead in 1943 and certified in 1950
rows.text: **This archive said** Anton Rudolf Defranceski, born 20 January 1890 at Klenovica house 22, **died in 1943** — recorded here «per the family». The same page also has him **on the Pfullingen list of foreigners in 1947** and **certified by that town's mayor in 1950**. **What is true** **Those cannot both be about the same living man.** Either the 1943 death is wrong — and it was only ever family testimony, never a register — or the Pfullingen documents are about a different Anton. The archive printed both and did not notice. **How it happened** Surfaced only because the family's oral history of **1948** made the widow's situation matter. Written up on Nineteen forty-eight, and the Crikvenica death register for 1943 is now an errand. **Lore is worth collecting partly because it makes you re-read your own pages.**

rows.what: What the first 403 actually was
rows.text:
**This archive said** That FamilySearch's tile server had **blocked** the death-register reading, recorded as `blocked` in the Search Register and written up on Method as a second instance of *when the service says stop, stop*.

**What is true** **The tile path was wrong.** Tiles live at `…/image.xml`'s sibling `image_files/{level}/{col}_{row}.jpg`, and the reader was asking for `…/{level}/{col}_{row}.jpg` — no `image_files`. Today that same wrong path returns a plain **404**; yesterday the security service answered the unknown path with a **403**. So the reading was stopped by **my own broken URL**, dressed up as somebody else's refusal.

A real block did come later, after several hundred tile requests, on `image.xml` itself — and *that* one is recorded honestly.

**How it happened** **Check that the request is well-formed before concluding you have been refused.** A 403 on a path that does not exist is not a verdict on your conduct. The cheap test — does the *correct* URL work? — costs one request and was not run.

rows.what: The FamilySearch paging cap
rows.text: **This archive said** A method note stated the persona endpoint caps out at about **1,100 records**. **What is true** The real ceiling is about **1,800**. The 1,100 figure came from a run that stopped early and was never retested; the full harvest of 10 September reached 1,800 distinct records before the endpoint began serving page one again. **How it happened** Retested deliberately, at offsets 1,800, 2,600 and 3,600, before publishing a number that the whole of The Register now rests on.

rows.what: Living people
rows.text:
**This archive said** The footer of every page read **«Living people are excluded from this build.»**

**What is true** At David's instruction the policy changed: living people the archive knows of are now named, **by name only** — no date of birth, no address, no place of residence, no photograph.

**How it happened** The footer was corrected the same day the policy changed, rather than left contradicting the pages above it.

rows.what: «Never once as the officiant»
rows.text:
**This archive said** That Don Stefano De Franceschi appears in the Vodnjan marriage register **nineteen times as a witness and never once as the officiant** — a point this archive made repeatedly, because it fixed his standing under the parroco Giovanni Tromba.

**What is true** On **26 January 1833** he married a couple himself: «**D.n Stefano De Franceschi, De Parochi lic., li congiunse e benedisse nella Chiesa Parrocchiale**».

**How it happened** True of every entry from 1819 to the end of 1832, and stated as though it were true of the whole book — while sixty openings of that book were still unread. **A claim about a register nobody has finished reading is a claim about the part you have read.** What survives is the better point: he acts «De Parochi lic.», by the parish priest's licence, exactly as at the baptism of 1816. Seventeen years apart, the same three words.

rows.what: Reading a formula as a personal arrangement
rows.text:
**This archive said** That «**De Parochi lic.**» — by the parish priest's licence — was the particular standing Don Stefano De Franceschi held at Vodnjan, and that the register used «the same three words about him» seventeen years apart, at a baptism in 1816 and at an altar in 1833.

**What is true** It is the register's **standard formula for any priest deputising for the parroco**. The very next entry, 13 February 1833, uses it of **Don Pietro Bradamante**.

**How it happened** Published the day before, on a run of entries that happened to feature one man. Two consecutive days of the same book undid it. The underlying fact is unchanged — Don Stefano was never the parson of Vodnjan — but the phrase was doing work it does not do.

rows.what: Full-text search of the whole book for every spelling of the surname
rows.src: Stjepan Antoljak, «Hrvati u prošlosti» (475 pp., supplied by David)
rows.text: **Two finds, and one of them is uncomfortable.** Antoljak cites Carlo De Franceschi twenty-one times across his study of the Slav settlement of Istria — and corrects him twice: once for misreading a charter («netočno pročitan»), once, harder, for writing in 1885 that Istria was never occupied or ruled by any Slav people, having confused the Rječina with the Raša. Published on Carlo's Book, under the claim it complicates. And, in the Zadar chapter, **a palace: «Ferro-Grisogono-Franceschi», on the corner of Široka ulica**, with a footnote to an article «Famiglia Franceschi» in the Zadar almanac for 1859 that this project had never heard of.

rows.what: A filter this archive had never applied to a query it had run many times
rows.src: FamilySearch personas, surname De Franceschi, Croatia, births 1600–1700
rows.text: **Seven records nobody here had seen, and three of them read on the film.** A De Franceschi household in **Fiume in 1626** — Giovanni Antonio and Lucia, three children baptised 1626, 1628 and 1632 — **113 years before the Valentino whom Kobler and Carlo took for the first of the name in the city**. The 1628 godfather is the imperial Captain of Fiume; the 1632 baptism was performed by the Bishop of Senj in person. Almost certainly not this family, and said so on the page. Also four unread: two at Omiš (1644, and a man born about 1581 who died in 1645) and two at Split.

rows.what: Opening the films behind four index entries this page had published as unread
rows.src: Omiš and Split parish registers — DGS 005494111 and 005494166
rows.text: Three of the four read. **Two index errors corrected** — the Omiš child of January 1644 is indexed «Nicolaa, Female» and the register says «il figlio … Nicolò»; the 1645 death is indexed 20 March and the register reads 29. **Two godparent appearances that exist in no index** — Sig.ra **Francesca de Franceschi** stands twice on one opening of the Omiš book. A father styled **Cap.n Zuane de Franceschi**. An **emergency baptism at Split in 1700**, «l'acqua in casa, in caso di necessità», to Egidio de Franceschi and Maria. And **Gioannes Maria de Franceschi, died 29 March 1645 aged 64** — born about 1581, the oldest birth year this archive holds for the surname anywhere in Croatia. The fourth, a Split burial of 1716, is still unopened and is labelled so.

rows.what: All 328 movement records harvested from the result listings (transcripts paywalled, none bought)
rows.text: **Four of the Eleven found in it, and one gravestone finished.** Bruno born 1907 petitions for United States citizenship at New York in 1939 and again in 1942 as «Bruno de Franceschi Or Seedorf»; Gerda born 1913 petitions in the same year — **the surname the Millbrook stone cut off is SEEDORF**. Antonio 1887 and Albina 1900 both cross in **1922**, brother and sister in the same year. Joseph 1892 petitions at New York in 1912, 1915 and 1916. Basilio, Dario and Benito all sail in 1955–56. And the shape of the whole file: **the commonest event is the same man arriving three times** — circulation, not emigration. Four Vermont border crossings point at the Barre granite sheds, which is where a stonecutter's sons would go. Published on Leaving.

rows.what: David took a trial and asked for everything; transcripts read, not just index rows
rows.src: Findmypast — full subscription, every category, every spelling
rows.text: **The American half of the family, in documents.** The 1930 census puts **three of the Eleven in one Brooklyn flat** — Albina, her husband Frank Chinkojan, and her brothers Anthony (immigrated 1922) and «Grochina», the enumerator's Gioacchino. **Albina's marriage licence of 23 April 1925 names her mother Maria Volhart**; Joseph's of 1926 names Maria Valbart; Bruno's of 1931 names Mary Walhal — three children, three clerks, one woman, and the parish book's Volhardt behind all of them. **Gerda's surname is Seedorf**, of Hanover. Joseph's 1917 draft card gives 12 March 1892 and «Frieste»; the 1940 census gives him a wife and two children; and a Sergeant Joseph De Franceschi of the First World War lies at Long Island National Cemetery, dead 26 April 1940, twenty-five days after that census. **Basilio died 15 June 1994.** And the fused spelling **Defranceski** returns thirty-six of its own — a family of five off the *Slovenija* at Philadelphia in 1954, and two graves at Horsham, Victoria.

rows.what: Searching the village name instead of the surname
rows.text: **«Gallignana» returns ten records in the whole database and three are this family's** — Joseph's naturalisation petition of 1915 and Albina's of 1928, both giving «Gallignana, Austria» as the birthplace in a United States federal record, and Albina's 1922 arrival. The other seven are the village's other emigrants: Poldrugovac, Millassich, Lanza, Silich. **«Pedena» and «Pisino» then gave the crossing**: Antonio and Albina De Franceschi, one index number apart, on the *Conte Rosso* out of Genoa in 1922 — he aged 35 living at **Pićan** with a wife **Marta** left behind, she aged 22 at Gallignana; and Albina's husband under a fourth spelling, **Frank Schinkopan of Pisino, born 24 February 1896**, naturalising at New York in 1920 and 1926.

rows.what: Opening the documents behind the transcripts: census sheet, naturalisation petitions and declarations
rows.src: Findmypast — the images, through the IIIF image service
rows.text: **An address, a ship and a date.** Albina's 1928 petition, in her own words: «I emigrated from **Genoa** on or about the **29 day of August 1922**, and arrived at the port of **New York** on the **9 day of September 1922**, on the vessel **Conte Rosso**» — and her residence, **2922 Ave. L, Brooklyn**, which is the house the 1930 census sheet shows the family **owning, valued at $16,000, with a radio**. The sheet also gives the trades: Frank Chinkojan a **chef**, Anthony a **fireman at an electric company**, and «Trochina» a **counter man in a restaurant, twenty-four weeks out of work** in the first spring of the Depression. Gerda's 1939 declaration carries her **photograph**, her arrival at New York on the **Dresden** from Bremen on **21 October 1929**, and the line «**he was born at Gallignana, Italy on August 12, 1907**». **And a correction**: the 1939 and 1942 records indexed under Bruno's name are Gerda's own papers. Two leads closed as well — Peter b.1902 was born at **Basel**, and the **1939 Register has no Defranceschi in England at all**.

rows.what: The certificate of arrival, the petition, and the Australian headstone
rows.src: Findmypast images, second pass — Joseph's naturalisation file; BillionGraves, Horsham
rows.text: **Joseph went first, and twelve years early.** His certificate of arrival, issued at Ellis Island on 2 December 1915: «Date of arrival **October 11, 1910** · Name of vessel **Martha Washington** · Line **Aus.-Amer.**» — out of **Trieste** about 24 September 1910, aged eighteen, on the Austro-Americana line. His petition gives **148 Sackett Street, Brooklyn**, on the docks, and an occupation this archive reads as **oiler**. **And the Horsham headstone is legible**: «IN LOVING REMEMBRANCE OF ZDRAVKO FRANK DEFRANCESKI · DIED 22ND DECEMBER 1979 AGED 58 · BELOVED HUSBAND OF ROSA», photographed 8 May 2018. The war-grave record for Sergeant Joseph De Franceschi is an index only — no image exists to open.

rows.what: Whether Antonio ever went back to the wife he left at Pićan
rows.src: Findmypast — the 1926 Martha Washington manifest, and a search for Marta
rows.text: **He did, and he came out again.** The manifest of the S.S. **Martha Washington** sailing from **Trieste**, stamped New York **31 May 1926**, line 6: «DEFRANCESCHI, ANTONIO, 39, married, **mason** … **last permanent residence N.Y., Brooklyn** … nearest relative in country whence came: **wife, Defranceschi Marta, Pedena 10, Istria, Italy**». «Last permanent residence Brooklyn» is a **returning resident** on a re-entry permit — so he had gone home to Istria between 1922 and 1926 and come back. **He was a mason**, the trade his father is given by in the Gračišće book of souls. And it is the ship **Joseph** crossed on in 1910. **Marta never came**: her only «record» carries the identifier one digit along from Antonio's — she is the relation field of his own manifest line. After April 1930 he appears in no American source at all, and never completed naturalisation.

rows.what: Seventy articles; the earliest sixty are shipping intelligence
rows.text: **A whole chapter nobody knew was there.** Between **1865 and 1878** a master of this name commands Austrian ships in the Black Sea grain and Bristol Channel coal trades — the ***Natalia*** out of Constantinople and Galatz, the ***Rachel*** from Odessa to Antwerp, the ***Peppina Luigia*** Trieste to Troon, and above all the ***Aquilone***, «**Aus, 350, Defranceschi**», tracked through nineteen printed sightings from Alexandria and Sulina to Belfast, Malta, Venice, Ghent, Barcelona and out of **Cardiff for Guadaloupe on 11 December 1877**. The masters printed beside him are Bujanovich, Lacovich, Cattarinich, Ivancich, Nicolich — **the sea-captain families of Lošinj, Rijeka and Bakar**, and this archive has an unplaced *Dominus* household at Bakar. And in 1896 the South Wales Echo writes that «**Signorina Defranceschi belongs to an old Cardiff family, and has recently taken her degree at the Vienna Conservatoire of Music**», playing harpsichord recitals at the Cardiff Exhibition. Published at **/at-sea/**.

rows.what: 83 more articles under the particle spelling, and one under the fused
rows.src: Findmypast newspapers, second pass — «de Franceschi» and «Defranceski»
rows.text: **Three more Aquilone voyages** (Queenstown with Alexandria wheat, 3 July 1872; **Leith for Trieste**, January 1874; Deal, Alexandria for Stockton, February 1875) — and a second man of the sea entirely: **«George De Franceschi, A.B., an Austrian»**, giving evidence at the Board of Trade inquiry into the loss of the Shields steamer *Aberlady Bay*, June 1889. The first man of this surname anywhere in the archive who is named, dated, put on a named ship and quoted. Also **Enrico de Franceschi, baritone of La Scala** — recorded 1924 with Zita Fumagalli-Riva («here is very excellent singing»), listed in 1926 among Amato, Galeffi, Rouard and Stracciari, and **broadcast live to Britain from La Scala in March 1938 with Gigli and Pagliughi**. And the single «Defranceski» hit fills in a career: **Josip Defranceski, Director of External Services, Radio Belgrade**, leaving Peshawar for Kabul in December 1959.

rows.what: The Aquilone's port of registry
rows.src: Lloyd's Register of Shipping, 1875 and 1877–78 (Internet Archive full text)
rows.text: **She is not in it.** Both volumes downloaded and searched in full; the only near match is the French *Aquilon* of Jersey, 48 tons. That is informative rather than disappointing: Lloyd's classed British ships and foreign ships whose owners paid London. **An Austrian barque of 350 tons belongs on the register of the Austro-Hungarian Veritas, whose books are at Trieste and Rijeka.** The port of registry — the fact that would say whether she was a Bakar, Rijeka or Lošinj ship — has to be asked there. What London gives instead is her Cardiff agent, **G. Montaldo & Co**.

rows.what: Gallignana, Pisino, Buccari as keywords
rows.src: British & Irish newspapers — the archive's own place-names
rows.text: **«Gallignana»: zero articles in the entire archive.** «Pisino»: 915, every one of them OCR noise — «early rising» mis-set, and a brand of stove polish called Pisino Sun. **«Buccari»: 1,377, and all of them shipping** — Bakar had its own standing heading in the London shipping press from at least 1850, between Cagliari and Carloforte in the alphabetical run of ports. The town where this archive has twelve unplaced *Dominus* people was tracked daily by the London insurance market for a century. **And no Defranceschi ever appears under that heading.**

rows.what: The Australian press, which is not on Findmypast
rows.src: Trove, National Library of Australia — newspapers and gazettes
rows.text: «Defranceski» returns **two**, both government gazettes. «Defranceschi» returns **thirteen**, and one is a story: *The Age*, Melbourne, **25 January 1954**, «Girl Saw Friend Drown» — «**Giordano Defranceschi, laborer**, swam out into the … but Defranceschi disappeared … **before the eyes of a girl he met here last week**.» The Australian inward passenger lists carry a **Giordano de Franceschi arriving in 1950**; this archive believes they are the same man and cannot prove it. Also **DeFranceschi Bros, 716 Chappie Lane, Broken Hill**, NSW Government Gazette, 17 June 1966. **And no nineteenth-century Defranceschi in the Australian press at all** — the name arrives after the Second World War, exactly as the passenger lists say.

rows.what: The one Australian record fifty-seven years before all the others
rows.src: NSW Unassisted Passenger Lists — the 1893 Australian outlier
rows.text: **Solved, and it is not a migrant.** «INWARD. A LIST of the Crew and Passengers arrived in the Ship **Miowera** of London, **James Stott** Master, of the Burthen of 1,911 Tons, from the Port of Melbourne to Sydney, New South Wales, 1893.» In the seamen's column, dittoed down from the quartermaster above him: «**G. Defranceschi · ″ · 28 · Austrian**». **Q.M. — quartermaster**, twenty-eight, Austrian, on the overnight run from Melbourne to Sydney on **6 January 1893**. He was not going to Australia; he was passing through it. The surname reaches Australia in 1893 as a sailor and does not settle there for another fifty-seven years.

rows.what: Albina's husband's own papers, and the 1922 embarkation list
rows.src: Findmypast images, third pass — Frank Schinkopan's declaration; the Conte Rosso manifest
rows.text: **Frank Schinkopan's declaration of intention, Brooklyn 1920**: «aged 24, occupation **Cook**, complexion fair, height 5 feet 8, weight 144, hair dark brown, eyes gray; **born in Pisino, Italy, on the 24 day of February 1896**; residing **304 Ninth Avenue, Brooklyn**; emigrated **from Trieste, Austria**, on the vessel *Elenor*; **not married**; renouncing particularly **Victor Emmanuel III, King of Italy, of whom I am now a subject**; arrived at the port of New York on or about the **15 March 1920**.» A cook in a Brooklyn room in 1920; a chef owning a $16,000 house on Avenue L by 1930. **And the Conte Rosso manifest opened** — the Italian form, «Numero dei biglietto · COGNOME E NOME · **PATERNITÀ** · ETÀ» — with **De Franceschi Antonio 35** and **De Franceschi Albina 22** on consecutive lines. **The paternità column is blank but for a tick**: the one document that asked directly who their father was did not write it down. A «going to join» column exists but the rows could not be aligned across the spread with certainty and were not guessed at.

rows.what: A death record for either of them
rows.src: Findmypast — deaths of Bruno and Gerda de Franceschi
rows.text: **Nothing.** Bruno died at Millbrook, New York, on 6 July 2000 by his gravestone, and the Social Security Death Index and obituary collections on Findmypast carry neither him nor Gerda. Their dates come from the stone and from the naturalisation papers, and that is where they stay.

rows.what: The last of the four unread records
rows.src: Split, Župa Sv. Dujma — DGS 005494174, image 378
rows.text: **The best single line found all day.** The index said «Nicolo De Franceschi, burial 18 May 1716, birth 1626». The register says: «**Can.co Don Nicolò de Franceschi** ⟨*Can.co di S. Vito di Candia*⟩ passò da questa alla miglior vita **d'anni 90 incirca** … et **fù sepolto nella Chiesa del Domo in Coro nella sepoltura delli Sig.ri Can.ci**.» **A canon of a church in Candia — Crete — buried in the choir of Split cathedral in the canons' vault, aged about ninety.** Born about 1626; Candia fell to the Turks in 1669 when he was forty-three. **The Seget branch's Cretan origin has been treated on this site as the family's own tradition. It now has a document standing beside it.**

rows.what: The Rovinj records, from 1619
rows.src: Rovinj, Župa Rovinj — DGS 005497871, images 225 and 466
rows.text: **A new earliest.** «**Adì 27 Mago 1619 · morì ser Piero di Franceschi da Pola. Fu portato il suo cadavere … off. L 24**» — the oldest dated appearance of this surname in Istria the archive holds, seven years before the Fiume baptisms and a hundred and forty-two before the name is first written at Gologorica. He is styled **ser**; he is **of Pola**, not of Rovinj; his **body was carried** there; and his offering of 24 lire is near the top of a page whose other entries run at 2, 6 and 12. **And the second-oldest is also a stranger**: «Ob.to di **Matt.o de Franceschi da Dignano**», 27 December 1728, 6 lire — Vodnjan, which this archive lists among the *unplaced*. The film holds fourteen more, including a Rovinj household across three generations (Giacomo → Vittorio & Domenica Moscarda → Piero Anto 1736) — **and Carlo De Franceschi's own marriage to Maria Michelcich, with his parents named as «Giuseppe da Gologorizza» and «Lambertina Pesle». That image has not been opened.**

rows.what: Finding and opening the registers, after this archive first said they did not exist
rows.src: Vodnjan (Dignano) parish registers — DGS 005497893–95, catalogue koha:963267
rows.text: **Found, and a correction retracted.** This archive said in the afternoon that the seventy-eight Vodnjan records were really Vižinada's, because the catalogue answered the film number 005497893 with «Župa Vižinada». **A reel can carry two parishes.** That one holds Vižinada's deaths 1754–1831 *and* **Vodnjan's baptisms 1815–1866**, catalogue item koha:963267 — «metrical books for the Roman Catholic congregation at **Dignano** … later **Vodnjan**». The marriages **1815–1884** and deaths to **1893** are on films 894 and 895. The baptismal book is headed «**LIBER BAPTIZATORUM IN ECCLESIA S. BLASII DIGNANI**», and entry 149 of **4 December 1816** gives house **376**, «**Pietro De Franceschi di Giuseppe, agricoltore**», «**Maria Malusà q.m Matteo di Antonio**», condition **civile** — and the baptising priest is «**D. Stefano De Franceschi, de Parocho licentia**». **A priest of the name at Vodnjan, and five lay households.** The one death on that reel, **Mathaeus De Franceschi son of Anton, house 32, 7 August 1819**, is in the *Liber Defunctorum of Castellier* — **Kaštelir, under Vižinada** — which is exactly why the wrong answer looked right.

rows.what: Reading the marriage register by eye, because nobody has indexed it
rows.text: **The register is not indexed.** Two hundred and eighty-six marriage-query arks were resolved against film 005497894 and **none** of them is on it, which is why these marriages have never been seen. Read opening by opening instead. Eleven openings in, **five De Franceschi appearances**: **30 March 1818, house 312 — «Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio. Maria, vedovo della q.m Veniera Franzin q.m Domenico», aged 42, marrying Lorenza Tesser q.m Ambrogio, widow of Andrea Manzin**, which puts his birth about 1776 and his father's death before 1818; **«+ Cristoforo De Franceschi di Giuseppe, tessitore»** and **«+ Pietro De Franceschi di Giuseppe, agricoltore»** as witnesses in March and September 1818, **both signing with a cross** — brothers, and a different Pietro from the widower; **«Don Stefano De Franceschi, Sacerdote»** as witness on 7 June 1819, with the page signed by **Giovanni Tromba S.T.D., parroco e preposito del Capitolo** — so Don Stefano was a priest of the town, not the parish priest; and **«la fu Domenica De Franceschi»**, mother of a bride aged 40 in November 1817, **dead before the register begins** and born about 1750. Images 183–265 still to read.

rows.what: Reading on: 1819 and 1820
rows.text: **A priest, a ploughman and a weaver turn out to be brothers.** On 17 August 1820 the clerk writes the witness in full — «**D.n Stefano De Franceschi *di Giuseppe* — Sacerdote**» — the same patronymic already recorded for «+ Pietro De Franceschi di Giuseppe, agricoltore» and «+ Cristoforo De Franceschi di Giuseppe, tessitore», both of whom sign with a cross. Don Stefano witnesses **four** marriages in these openings (7 June and 20 August 1819, 17 August and 13 November 1820), twice beside a canon of the chapter, never as officiant — the parroco who signs every page is **Giovanni Tromba S.T.D.** Also found: **«la vivente Antonia Maria De Franceschi»**, widow of Damiano Storcovich, alive 30 June 1819 with a daughter aged 40 — a **second** woman of the name born about 1750, alongside the Domenica already dead in 1817.

rows.what: The 1821 marriage that closes a chain
rows.text: **Four generations off one page.** From 1821 the register rules new columns — «Sponsus **et Genitores**» — and names both parties' parents in every entry. The first result: 9 June 1821, house 356, «**Gio: Maria De Franceschi figlio di Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria e della fu Veniera Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel**», aged 22, marrying **Lucia Bonassin**, aged 27. That is the household this archive had reconstructed from the baptism register — now with its father, grandfather and great-grandfather named. It also **settles this morning's open question**: the Gio Maria fathering children in the 1820s was flagged as probably a grandson of the Gio Maria dead by 1818, marked inf because it was not proved. It is proved.

**A third De Franceschi woman married out.** 14 November 1821, house 54: Maria, daughter of Alvise Birattan q.m Saba and **«Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro»**, marries at twenty-one — so Lucia married by 1799 and her father Pietro was dead by 1821, which makes him **older than the Pietro who remarried in 1818**. The witnesses are **Giannandrea Dalla Zonca, Nobile** and **Guglielmo Conte Lombardo di Pola**, and the couple needed a dispensation in the fourth degree of consanguinity. Also **Don Stefano's fifth witness appearance**, 3 July 1822, house 200. And one deliberate miss recorded — «Maddalena **Franceschich** q.m Gio, di Pinguente», a Slavic patronymic out of Buzet that is not this surname.

**«Pietro De Franceschi di Gio., da Dignano — Tessitore»**, witness on 30 January 1824 at a marriage celebrated in **Šišan** by that village's curate. Because the wedding was outside Vodnjan the clerk records where each witness came from, and this is the same formula that labelled «Matt.o de Franceschi **da Dignano**» when he was buried at Rovinj in 1728 — ninety-six years apart, the name written down only from outside the town. He is a **fourth distinct Pietro** — son of a Giovanni, and a weaver like Cristoforo. Also **Bianca Bortolan, second daughter of Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro**, married 14 June 1824 aged 20, fixing that household's dates without a baptism surviving for any of them.

rows.what: 1823–1824: a second male line
rows.text: **A second Vodnjan line, three generations deep, unrelated to Giuseppe's.** 19 November 1823, house 684: **Bonetta, «figlia del fu Pietro De Franceschi q.m Dom.co e Domenica Manzin q.m Dom.co»**, marries at twenty-three — so born about 1800, her father dead by 1823 and **his** father a **Domenico**. Ninety days later, 28 February 1824, house 764, a **«Pietro De Franceschi q.m Pietro, agricoltore»** witnesses — a man whose father Pietro is newly dead, and on the dates almost certainly Bonetta's brother. Left open on purpose: whether this Pietro q.m Domenico is also the «q.m Pietro» who fathered Lucia, married out by 1799. A shared forename is not evidence.

rows.what: 1824–1825, and a correction
rows.text: **A third daughter, and a misreading put right.** 15 January 1825, house 667: **Lucia, «figlia di Alvise Birattan q.m Saba e di Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro»**, marries at 28 — born about 1797, alongside Maria (b. c.1800) and Bianca (b. c.1804). Three weddings out of one house, none of them indexed anywhere. This entry also writes the husband's surname clearly, and it is **Birattan**, not the **Bortolan** this archive published earlier today off the 1821 hand; the earlier rows have been corrected in place with the change stated. Also **Don Stefano's sixth witness appearance**, 28 October 1824, house 208, again beside Canon Michiel Benedetto.

**Pietro had a brother.** 25 January 1826, house 224: Michiela, «figlia di **Cristoforo De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria** e di Maria Luigia Manzin q.m Domenico», marries at 26 — the same dead father as the Pietro who remarried in 1818, so **Cristoforo is his brother** and the eldest Vodnjan line now carries two sons. It also means **two men named Cristoforo De Franceschi are alive in the town at once** — this one q.m Gio: Maria, and the weaver di Giuseppe — told apart only by the father's name. And 10 July 1826: **«Ant.o De Franceschi fu Vittorio»** witnesses at a wedding celebrated by the archpriest **at Svetvinčenat** — a Rovinj given-name in the patronymic and a Svetvinčenat venue, recorded as a coincidence of the page and **not** claimed as a link. One miss ruled out by eye on image 196: «Pietro **Francin** q.m Fran.co», not Franceschi.

**A sister, and the eldest line becomes a family of three.** 7 February 1828, house 366: Michiela Damiana, daughter of the late Domenico Pastrovicchio and **«della vivente Veniera De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria»**, marries at twenty — and the witness is **«Cristoforo De Franceschi fu Gio: M.a, Agricoltore»**, her uncle. So Gio. Maria De Franceschi, dead before 1818, is now shown with **three children — Pietro, Cristoforo and Veniera** — none of whom has a baptism on any film this archive can reach; the register found them by naming their dead father the same way three times across ten years. Also **«Pietro De Franceschi di Gio., Tessitore»** witnessing again on 23 September 1828, in Vodnjan this time and without the «da Dignano», which shows he lived there. And **Don Stefano's seventh and eighth appearances**, 16 February and 23 September 1828. Images 199 and 200 read with no De Franceschi on them.

rows.what: Late 1828 into 1829
rows.text: **Cristoforo the weaver, named in full at last** — «Cristoforo De Franceschi **di Giuseppe**, Tessitore», witness 25 November 1828 — which is what safely separates him from the other Cristoforo, *fu Gio: Maria*, the ploughman who witnessed his own niece's wedding ten months earlier. Two men, one name, one town, one volume. **Don Stefano witnesses twice more the same afternoon** (entries 42 and 43, both 25 November 1828), taking him to ten. And the near-miss worth keeping: «Giuseppe figlio del fu **Pietro Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel**» — not Franceschi, but the **identical patronymic** to Pietro De Franceschi's first wife «Veniera Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel», so this groom is Veniera's nephew and a first cousin of the 1821 bridegroom. Francin is not Franceschi, and in this parish the two families are a household deep in each other. Image 204 read clean.

**Don Stefano reaches fourteen witness appearances in ten years** — four of them on these two openings alone (23 May, 31 August, 19 and 22 December 1829). The May wedding was held in the **church of San Martino** and he stood beside **Ferdinando Verbits, Maestro delle Scuole Elementari**, the town schoolmaster; the December one carried a dispensation from the three readings of the banns granted by the **Imperial-Royal Circle Captaincy**. He is never once the officiant: that is always the parroco Giovanni Tromba. **Pietro De Franceschi di Gio., Tessitore** witnesses a third time on 22 February 1830, on a marriage dispensed in the fourth degree of consanguinity by the **Ordinariate of Pola** — which is where Vodnjan's church paperwork ran, and where to write next.

rows.what: 1830, and a fifth generation
rows.text: **A widow's second wedding names her grandfather.** 25 June 1830, house 483: **Veniera De Franceschi**, widow of Domenico Pastrovicchio, remarries at forty-nine — and because a widow's remarriage is written out in full, the clerk records her parents: **«Gio. Maria De Franceschi *fu Pietro* e Michiela Zambaletta fu Cristoforo»**. The father who has been a bare name since March 1818 now has a father and a wife of his own, and the Vodnjan line stands **five generations deep** off this one unindexed book, back to a marriage of the 1770s. **Michiela Zambaletta is the first woman named as a mother anywhere in the line.** Don Stefano witnesses twice more, 8 June and 24 November 1830, reaching sixteen.

rows.what: Whose face is on the Crikvenica page
rows.src: Family photograph collection — the hand-tinted portrait pair
rows.text: **The face was wrong, and it was on the direct line's own page.** A hand-tinted portrait of a bearded man in a bow tie had been published here as **Josip Defranceschi, born at Gračišće 22 March 1863** — David's great-grandfather, and the only likeness the direct line had. **David identified it: the photograph is from the Imotski branch**, and the sitter is a Josip of that family. Two branches' pictures sit in one collection; a card carried the name, this line has a man of that name, and this archive matched face to name without asking which Josip. The register plates on that page were checked against Gračišće and Ledenice — **the portrait was never checked against anything.** Withdrawn from the head card and from the 1906 entry in the story, recaptioned in the gallery, and a correction section added to the page where it stood. The companion portrait published as his wife Ana is **also withdrawn**: its only identification was that it matched the man beside it. **No likeness of the Crikvenica Josip is known to this archive.** Note the pattern — the retired 2018 GEDCOM spliced Imotski onto this line too. The same seam has now caught this archive twice, once in a pedigree and once in a photograph.

rows.what: Carlo De Franceschi's own marriage, opened at last
rows.text: **The historian was married lying down.** 1 March 1852 at Rovinj: «Il Signor **Carlo De Franceschi q.m Giuseppe e della Sig.ra Lambertina Pesle di Mattia, da Gologorizza di Pisino, Assessore presso quest'I. R. Corte di Giustizia**, celibe d'anni 40» marries «**Maria Michelcich di Luca e di Maria**, celibe d'anni 26» — **«al letto dello Sposo, per essere gravemente ammalato»**, at the bridegroom's bed because he was gravely ill. The banns were **dispensed the same day by the Imperial-Royal District Captaincy, note № 898, *urgente necessitate***, and the witnesses are the **deputy State Prosecutor Zaccaria Maver** and **Dr Barzan, physician** — the law and the medicine, not the family. He did not die; he lived to 1893. The entry also fixes his office in 1852 and names both parents. Two corrections fall out: the register says **d'anni 40** and he was **forty-two** (b. 16 Oct 1809); and this archive's marriage table carried the year as **1812** — it is **1852**, now fixed with the reason stated. On the same film, a burial of «Julius, son of Carlo», born 1853, dead 13 February 1854 — very probably the first child of this marriage.

**A fifth woman married out, and a fourth trade.** 17 November 1831: «Ant.o Gio., figlio di Fran.co Gorlato q.m Biaggio e della **q.m Luigetta De Franceschi**», marrying at twenty-three — so she was born about 1808's mother's generation and dead by 1831, and she joins Domenica, Antonia Maria, Lucia and Veniera as women of the name recoverable only through a child's wedding. 18 February 1832: **«Giovanni De Franceschi q.m Pietro, Calzolajo»** witnesses — a shoemaker, and on the patronymic very likely a brother of Bonetta and of Pietro the ploughman in the line descending from a Domenico. **Pietro q.m Pietro** also witnesses again, 15 October 1831. Don Stefano reaches **eighteen**. One generation of one surname in one small town now shows a **priest, a ploughman, a weaver and a shoemaker**.

rows.what: A face on the direct line
rows.text:
**This archive said** A hand-tinted portrait of a bearded man in a bow tie, published as **Josip Defranceschi, born at Gračišće 22 March 1863** — David's great-grandfather, and the only likeness the direct line had.

**What is true** It is from the **Imotski** branch, and the sitter is a Josip of that family. **No likeness of the Crikvenica Josip is known to this archive.** The companion portrait published as his wife Ana is withdrawn too, because its only identification was that it matched the man beside it.

**How it happened** Two branches' photographs sit in one family collection. A card carried the name, this line has a man of that name, and this archive matched the face to the name without asking which Josip — while checking every register plate on the same page against Pazin and Ledenice. **The portrait was never checked against anything.** Identified by David, who holds the originals. The retired 2018 GEDCOM spliced Imotski onto this line as well: the same seam has caught this archive twice.

rows.what: Seventy-eight records moved to the wrong parish
rows.text:
**This archive said** That the seventy-eight Vodnjan records were **really Vižinada's**, because resolving them to film 005497893 and asking the catalogue who made that film returned «Rimokatolička crkva. Župa Vižinada».

**What is true** **A reel can carry more than one parish.** That one holds Vižinada's deaths 1754–1831 *and* **Vodnjan's baptisms 1815–1866** (koha:963267). The records are Vodnjan's.

**How it happened** The catalogue answers a film-number query with the **first creator on the reel**. The method was sound and the question put to it was wrong. It stood on the site for about an hour, published within twenty minutes of being reached and **without a single image being opened**. What made it look right: the one death on that reel really is Vižinada's — it is in the *Liber Defunctorum of Castellier*, Kaštelir.

rows.what: Forty-four people filed under the wrong town
rows.text:
**This archive said** Eight reconstructed Vodnjan households and their children carried **Vižinada** as their parish in the roster, and the households themselves had no place at all.

**What is true** They are Vodnjan. Eight households placed, **forty-four rows moved**, and Vodnjan moved out of *unplaced* into Southern Istria.

**How it happened** The correction above was published on the narrative page and **never reached the data**. David asked why the headcount had not moved all day; it had not, because the roster was three commits behind the research and still carried the error the essay had already retracted. Fixed, and the rebuild order is now written into the queue notes.

**This archive said** Carlo De Franceschi × Maria Michelcich, **1812**.

rows.what: A broken site pushed live
rows.text:
**This archive said** Nothing — the page simply was not there for about six minutes.

**What is true** The build had failed and the commit went out anyway.

**How it happened** `npm run build | tail -2` hides the build's exit code behind the pipe's. **This was the second time.** There is now `scripts/publish.sh`, which builds without a pipe, checks that every source page produced an output file, and refuses to commit or push if either fails.

rows.what: Bold words breaking onto their own line
rows.text:
**This archive said** Nothing wrong in the words — but wherever a paragraph of running prose contained a **bold phrase**, the phrase was thrown onto a line of its own, so the sentence read as three broken fragments.

**What is true** A styling fault, live across the site for an unknown period and on eleven pages that pass marked-up text into a paragraph.

**How it happened** `.prose` was declared `display:flex; flex-direction:column`, which turns every inline child — including a `<strong>` — into its own flex item. It is now spacing applied between block children only. Found by looking at a new page rather than by any test. Two stylesheets exist in this repo and only one is loaded; the first fix went into the wrong one.

rows.what: Counting records by place, with a parameter that does not count
rows.text:
**This archive said** Per-place record counts for this surname across sixty Istrian and Kvarner towns, and a research queue carrying «Vižinada — 53 records, unread», «Draguč — 25», «Dubrovnik — 38».

**What is true** **The place parameter on this search endpoint does not filter.** Ten values were tested, including «Zzzznowhere» and «Atlantis», and every one returned the same total: **3,652**. Vižinada and Draguč return identical result sets. Dubrovnik returns the unfiltered list. The queued «Vižinada 53» records are on the **Vodnjan** film and have already been read.

**How it happened** The parameter is a relevance boost dressed as a filter — no error, no warning, just the whole set back in a different order. The sweep survives because its method independently checked each record's own place text before counting it; the **queue did not**, and carried three phantom tasks for days. The reliable route is to resolve records to their film and read the catalogue's item list — remembering that a film can carry more than one parish.

rows.text: Standing rules, so nothing here can ever be mistaken for a source: no invented face is ever captioned with a real person's name; no invented lettering on a real inscribed stone and no invented heraldry for a family whose arms are documented; every image captioned as a constructed illustration with its departures from the record named; no fabricated documentary apparatus — no title block, scale bar, dimension, survey date; the unaltered original archived in the source library beside its brief, marked with whatever was removed. Briefs at notes/image-prompts.md. ALL EIGHT NOW DONE, seven published: the house at Gologorica, with the 1711 tablet deliberately blank; Imotski 1717; the road of the Furlans 1679; the Salamon palace; the mills at Perinuša; Crikvenica in the winter of 1943; Pfullingen 1944. Plus a lapidarius of Gračišće, published as the trade and explicitly NOT as a portrait of Antonio, because the model gave it a detailed invented face. TWO WITHHELD: the first Gologorica house, which carried a fabricated pseudo-Latin inscription across the 1711 tablet; and a close detail of the arms and the Madonna relief, because the coat of arms in it does not match the blazon Carlo gave Kobler and the carving the family photographed — a cross crossed by two arrows over a pomegranate. Both kept in the library marked WITHHELD. Four failure modes, each seen more than once: a caption burned into the picture; a watermark; an invented inscription or coat of arms on a real carved stone; and an image returned dressed as a measured conservation survey of a real protected building, with title block, scale bar, dimensions and date. Every one of them was caught before publication.

Four things were genuinely new: the byname «Franceschi dalle Rose»; a German branch route Ližnjan → Monheim with a «Grga» who died at Zagreb and a Petar at Metzingen, four kilometres from Pfullingen; a layer of forty-four Veneto emigration hotspots ending at São Paulo, which is a candidate departure region for the Brazilian cluster this archive has never had one for; and two Dalmatian names, Tomasso and a Francesca de Franceschi of the 1500s. The whole capture is in the source library under «oldsite».

rows.text: 127 entries of the surname at Ližnjan, 1788 onward. Grga is real: Gregorius Defranceski, aged 22 at his marriage on 10 June 1874, so born 1851, son of Gregorio Defranceschi and Agata Skifić, husband of Maria Vojnić, father of Anastasia (1875 and 1876), Maria (1878), Justina (1879), Maria (1882) and Josephus (1887). His daughter Justina married Josephus Fedel on 22 Nov 1898 and a Stana married Jacobus Vojnić on 7 Aug 1899 — Fedel and Vojnić being two of the surnames standing beside «Defrančeski Ante» in the Ližnjan subscription list of 1920. Behind Gregorio stands a Mattio De Franceschi and a Madalena Peucovich. Index entries only; the books are at Pazin and unread.

rows.text: Nothing for either. The Monheim pin is Monheim in the Donau-Ries, not Monheim am Rhein — about a hundred kilometres from Metzingen, and Metzingen is four from Pfullingen. Both the Monheim line and «Grga dies in Zagreb» carry no note, no date and no document on the map they came from, and neither could be confirmed here. The nearest thing is a Zagreb grave for Marija Defrančeski, 1884–1971, two years off Grga's daughter Maria of 1882 — suggestive, not proof, and left as such.

The direct line agrees wherever both hold a fact, and the tree supplies what this archive lacked: exact death dates for Antonius (4 Aug 1894) and for Giovanni Battista (14 Sep 1846), Gologorica rather than Gračišće as the 1787 birthplace, and an ark for the 1750 Giovanni that no page had ever been put in front of. rows.text: A departure region for the Brazilian cluster, which this archive has never had. Scorzè, Moniego (Noale), Cornedo Vicentino, Castelgomberto and Pederobba in the Veneto — with «DE FRANCESCHI Luigi, spouse BAROLO Caterina Luigia, from Moniego, Noale, Venezia to São Paulo» and «Giuseppe Romano De Franceschi, born Scorzè 22 May 1835, died Moniego». And a second region entirely: the Castelnuovo pin is Castelnuovo in the Valsugana, Trentino — four kilometres from Telve, where David's tree holds eighteen people of this surname. The São Paulo destinations are all coffee-belt, which is a different and later migration from the Rio Grande do Sul colonies of 1875. Brazil is two stories, not one. Also on those layers: Castelnovo del Friuli to Trostberg in Bavaria (Peter DeFranceschi b. 19 Feb 1841); Mione to Biella; Bishop Lucio Soravito de Franceschi of Adria-Rovigo; and a France cluster around Metz, Nancy, Fréjus and Propriano.

rows.what: The Grand Chancellor's portraits — Detroit, Hampton Court, Washington — and the 2016 Artibus et Historiae paper
rows.text: Closed as far as it can be from here, after a year on the roadmap. Grand Chancellor of Venice 1529 to his death in 1551; Titian's friend; painted into the «Presentation of the Virgin» in the Accademia; owned two portraits of himself by Titian, the head in both taken from Titian's own picture now in Detroit. The Hampton Court double portrait was cleaned in 1958 and gave up a third figure painted out earlier. The National Gallery of Art in Washington holds a further portrait it declines to call Titian. Not kin, and never claimed as such. Still unread: Charles Hope's «Titian's portraits of Grand Chancellor Andrea de' Franceschi», Artibus et Historiae 74 (2016), 139–151 — the academia.edu copy sits behind Cloudflare. The National Gallery of Art site requires JavaScript and the National Trust site served a CAPTCHA; neither was circumvented, and the facts above come from those institutions' own catalogue text as quoted elsewhere.

rows.what: The fifteenth-century Venetian painter carried on the roadmap as unfinished
rows.text: Active 1443–1468, birth and death unknown. Religious work on church commission; the style follows Michele Giambono and he may have worked with Antonio Vivarini. An altarpiece of 1447 in the Museo Civico at Padua; a St Mary Magdalen and a St Catherine of Alexandria in the Ashmolean at Oxford; a St Michael the Archangel and a St Mamas series. Not kin — two and a half centuries before this family reaches Istria. Roadmap item closed.

The byname «dalle Rose» belongs to the Donà — the Donà dalle Rose, a Venetian noble house with origins in Romagna and Altinum, two Doges, and a surviving main branch whose archive is at the Museo Correr. The pin's Ravenna-to-Venice sequence is the Donà origin story. Recorded as a probable conflation so that it is not repeated.

rows.what: 491 images from six visits — Carnia (Ovaro, Mione, Muina, Agrons), Gologorica house and graves, Gračišće, Seget and Umag, Crikvenica–Klenovica–Novi–Senj, and the Pazin reading room — read as contact sheets so that the frames worth publishing can be chosen
rows.text: Read as contact sheets and plated. **31 published so far.** Gologorica (11): the builder's tablet, the memorial to Carlo, the arms cartouche with the Madonna aedicule beneath it, the blazon in the tomb pediment and the same arms weathered nearly smooth on an older stone, the tomb, the house from the lane, the arcaded end with the number 22, a wall niche, a carved ring, the chapel. Carnia (10): SORAVITO DE FRANCESCHI cut in stone at Ovaro with Anna Crosilla his widow; De Franceschi Ugo 1930–2020; Antonio 1877–1962 with Marta Anzola dead at twenty-five; Gio. Batta 1880–1963; Francesco 1887–1945; an 1850s stone; the war memorial carrying Vittorio and Isidoro De Franceschi; the campanile of Santa Maria di Gorto over the graves — the pieve whose parishes drew up the 1679 return. Gračišće (3): «F DE FRANCESCHI» with Marfan Virginija and Nazarijo; the Salamon grave, which turns Francisca Salamon from a surname into a family still in that ground; and a Marfan stone. Umag and Seget (7): the tomb's blue-and-gilt ironwork lunette with a lion rampant beneath a star under a coronet — the other family's arms, against Gologorica's cross, arrows and pomegranate; «FAMIGLIA DE FRANCESCHI — SEGHETTO»; «FAMIGLIA ETTORE DE FRANCESCHI»; a stone of 1848; the house at Seget; the tomb whole; the pine-cone finial. Living people appear in many frames and are excluded throughout. Klenovica and the coast (6): «OBITELJ DEFRANCESKI» with three portrait medallions — the household under the name it took on the coast — and then the Kalanj, who are everywhere in that ground: Marija 1889–1970, Josip, Franjo and Zora on one stone, Rozalija Anton Marija and Milan on another, Vinko and Paulina, Tomislav, Marijan, and the Kalanj-Perković. Anton Rudolf's mother was Ana Kalanj of Klenovica house 22, and it is her family and not his that stayed. Also a partisan star laid in white stone among the graves. **39 field plates published across six places.** The Pazin reading-room set of 117 is register images rather than ground; two of them are now published on The Eleven — the Gračišće Status Animarum for house 24, which carries the midwife Maria Fernazar's household, the eleven children in one column, and Daniel's household beneath. That page also settled Josip's birth at 22 March 1863 and joined Basilio of New York to this line.

Luster u Senju». The 1951 certificate was new, and carries the word STATELESS against the father in his own country. rows.text: **Settled, and the answer is that they are not online.** FamilySearch's Crikvenica holding, catalogue item 522842, gives its own coverage in the film notes: **Rođeni 1859–1896**, Vjenčani 1859–1908, Umrli 1859–1892 and 1893–1908. The births stop in 1896 and the other two series run twelve years further. The same cut is on every parish along that coast — Senj births end 1894 with marriages to 1920, Bribir births end 1886, Grižane 1886. It is the hundred-year rule as it stood when the films were made. The family's own photographs stop at 1896 because they were taken from the film. FamilySearch full-text search — which does read unindexed images — holds **no Croatian church-book collection**; its nearest are Italian civil registration and a Zadar-only Dalmatian births series. ARHiNET is gone: NAIS was retired in June 2020 for HAIS, and hais.arhiv.hr resolves but times out from here. **The next step is a letter to the Župni ured at Crikvenica or to the Rijeka archdiocese, not another search.**
