rows.src: FamilySearch full-text search — the unindexed-image corpus
rows.text: **3,965 hits for «Defranceschi» across 172 collections, and not one of them is Croatian.** The corpus is Italian civil registration, the Americas, and a Dalmatian births series that turns out to be Zadar only. That is the negative this archive needed before writing letters. It is also a lead: **«Italy, Trieste, Trieste, Civil Registration (Tribunale), 1924–1939» carries 53 Defranceschi**, with Padova 143, Bologna 501 and Treviso 7 beside it. Trieste 1924–1939 is the right city and the right years for the Istrians who left through it, and this archive has never read a line of it.

rows.what: The finding aid at arhiv.hr, searched for Crikvenica and Proložac across all seven kinds of register. This collection filmed the parish offices and the civil registry offices as well as the state archives, so it is not bound by the cut that ends FamilySearch's Croatian birth registers in the 1880s and 1890s
rows.src: HR-HDA-1448 — the Croatian State Archives' supplementary register microfilms
rows.text: **The single most useful thing found for this archive in weeks, and it is a catalogue rather than a record.** For Crikvenica it lists births to **1948**, marriages to **1947**, deaths to **1928**, and — this is the one — a **Status animarum of the twentieth century**, roll ZM-34J/251, mark M-5976, digitised, from the Župni ured Crikvenica. A Status animarum lists a house, its head, his wife and every child with a birth date; it is the form that gave this archive the whole of Gračišće house 24 in one opening. Crikvenica births 1897–1908 are absent here too and may not survive, but the household book and the marriage register of 1909–1947 between them should answer the three unaccounted names on the Crikvenica monument without the baptisms at all. Proložac, the Imotski family's own parish, runs unbroken 1853–1949 with everything from 1892 digitised. Ordered by e-mail to info@arhiv.hr quoting place, kind, period, roll signature and topographic mark; read in the HDA reading room, ten units a day. **Nothing has been read yet — this is the list of what exists and where.**

rows.what: The two non-Istrian houses of the surname, researched past the secondary accounts this site had been using: the 2016 conservation study of Stancija Seget, the Istrian encyclopaedia, and the Franciscan province of Split's own histories of its Omiš and Imotski convents
rows.src: Seget and Imotski, taken back to the sources
rows.text: **Seget:** the house carries its own dates — «1724» on the courtyard portal and «1732» with the initials «MA. F.» on the cistern, Marc'Antonio's monogram on his own well-head. A generation appears that this archive had never printed: **Giorgio de Franceschi, 1788–1865**, who threw a staircase block along the east front in **1843–45** and put a classicist façade over it, frescoed inside by **Michele Urban**, the architect to be sought among those practising at Trieste. The estate's economy turns from wine to olive oil about 1840. And the Venier–Valier disagreement is settled for Venier, from 1623. **Imotski:** four corrections. The friars were not at Proložac village but **on an islet in Prološko blato from about 1600**, marked by a stone cut A.D. 1609. The party Zuane sheltered was **fifteen people of whom nine were friars**, with a lay brother, four schoolboys and a hermit. Skalice at Omiš was begun **13 July 1716** and blessed **29 October 1718** on ground belonging to Pavao Despotović and Jakov Mariani. And **the friars did not return in 1717 — they returned in 1738**, building at Imotski from 1740. Zuane's own dates are 1673–1741. **And one unopened primary source:** at Skalice there is a book bound in sheepskin, written in bosančica on 416 leaves, which is the friars' own chronicle of the flight. It is in a friary, not an archive. **And then the thesis was read.** David cleared the repository's bot check himself, and «Uloga obitelji Franceschi u mletačkom osvajanju Imotskog» — Matea Kaćunić, Split, September 2025, 77 pages, open access — turns out to be the best single source on the Dalmatian family that exists. It corrects this archive six times and adds a second estate. Full account on the Imotski page; the PDF is now in this project's library.

rows.what: The first unindexed FamilySearch register image this archive has read at full resolution, rather than through the viewer's shrunken view — Imotski-Glavina, Atti di Morte, third quarter 1845
rows.src: The Imotski death register, read off the page
rows.text: **Entry 17. «Franceschi Domenica», 48, Cattolica, «Moglie di q.m Giovanni Vucemilovich» — and in the PATRIA column, «Nata in ALMISSA, domiciliata in IMOSCHI».** Almissa is Omiš. Her parents are given as «q.m Vicenzo Franceschi, q.m Antonia Cappelletti»; she died at three in the morning of 10 August 1845 in her husband's house of chronic gastritis, was seen by the district surgeon Ravlin on the 11th and buried the same day in the town cemetery of Imotski, by fra Bernardino Brajković. **That is the join between the Omiš branch and the Imotski household, in a parish register.** The method is the other half of the finding and it is reusable: FamilySearch serves each image as a Deep Zoom pyramid, and from a signed-in session the tiles of any chosen rectangle can be composed at true resolution — a 6180 × 4247 master read as clearly as the open book, instead of the 600-pixel view the ordinary viewer gives. Written up on the Parish Books page. **Every unindexed volume this archive has listed is now actually readable.**

rows.src: Donji Proložac, deaths 1837–1859 — swept page by page
rows.text: **No Franceschi and no Frančeski in twenty-two years of that parish's dead.** The surnames are Šegarić, Prlina, Ćurić, Grizinić, Zorko, Martinis, Vlašanović, Smoljan, Dujmović, Babajko, Točina, Fazinić, Kosulić, Šimac, Marinović, Rosulić, Šinožić — a Croatian peasant parish with no Italian household in it, and the names do not change even when the register itself switches from Italian to Croatian in the 1850s. One near miss checked and discarded: «Maria Martinna Franinacich», image 74. **A complete negative is worth more here than a hit would have been**: it says the family were not parishioners of Proložac, so the stone is either later than 1859 or belongs to someone brought there — and there is a reason they would be brought there, because their own church at Opačac is in the immediate vicinity of the village. Next: Imotski deaths after 1851, and the Proložac deaths from 1859 on, which are not on FamilySearch but are digitised on HDA rolls ZM-34F/1118 and ZM-34F/1119.

rows.what: A 160-page brief written for the Paris Peace Conference by a member of the Yugoslav delegation, with a documentary appendix of Fiume's nineteenth-century election papers. Read in full for the surname and for the Istrian and Kvarner place-names
rows.src: Šišić, «An Abridged Political History of Rieka (Fiume)», Paris 1919
rows.text: **One hit in a hundred and sixty pages, and it is the right one.** Appendix XVIII, the protocol of the electoral committee of Fiume's second college, 20 April 1871: the assessors are «Signor Francesco Defranceschi» and Francesco Seemann under president Pietro Dabalà, and the protocol is signed at the foot **«Frco Defranceschi»**. 128 of 1,115 electors voted; 126 chose Dr Antonio Randich to replace the resigning Giovanni de Ciotta in the Croatian-Slavonian Diet. Almost certainly Kobler's Francesco Giuseppe de Franceschi, patrician councillor and royal harbourmaster, of the stock that came «da Pisino» — which is the County of Pazin, which is where this archive's own villages are. Written up on the Kobler page. It also names a source worth chasing: the Fiume electoral roll of 1871.

rows.what: A civil-engineering journal's architectural survey of the fortified places north of the Čepić field, including Gologorica building by building — supplied by the family
rows.src: Regan & Nadilo, «Istarski kašteli … sjeverno od Čepićkog polja», Građevinar 2012
rows.text: **A hard date for the lease, and a name for the relief.** The Gologorica benefice was founded in **1443** by the Pazin provost Andreas Schuel; Frederick III took the right of appointment; the holders were the captains of Pazin and the bishops of Pedena, then the Marquis de Prié, then Charles Antoine Biotz, and «**naposljetku od 1772. obitelj De Franceschi … do ukidanja feudalnih odnosa 1848**» — the De Franceschi held it on lease from **1772 to 1848**, seventy-six years. That fits Carlo's «affitto fermo» rather than contradicting it, and dates it. The house is described as «velika kamena palača obitelji De Franceschi, dvokatna građevina s balkonom i portalom iz 1711., ukrašena grbom i natpisom te **reljefom s prikazom Isusa**» — which settles a thing this site once got wrong: the relief over the door is a figure of Christ, and it is real. Also: Gologorica burned in 1463, 1508 and 1511; the bell tower finished 1740; an Imago pietatis of 1446 and a Glagolitic inscription of 1595 in the parish church; and **Mikula Gologorički**, priest of this parish, wrote the Croatian Glagolitic version of the Istrian Boundary Settlement of 1325.

rows.what: Šišić's Fiume brief of 1919; Regan and Nadilo's architectural survey of the Istrian castles; a Croatian historiography syllabus; Belaj on sacred triangular structures; and Orbanić in Acta Histriae 32 (2024)
rows.src: Four more PDFs from the family, September 2026
rows.text: **Three yields, one modest, one nothing.** Šišić gives a Francesco Defranceschi signing a Fiume election protocol in 1871. Regan and Nadilo date the Gologorica benefice lease to **1772–1848** and name the relief over the door as a figure of Christ. **Orbanić is the most valuable of the four, and not for its subject.** Its source list cites «Župni arhiv Gologorice, Matična knjiga krštenih 1691–1763» and «Matična knjiga umrlih 1646–1777» — **the Gologorica parish registers, in the parish, being read by a historian in 2024.** This archive has been saying they are the great absence in every collection it has searched. They exist, and the deaths start in 1646. It also gives Petar Kruzila, parish priest there 1722–31, deaf from a fall for doubting a miracle. The historiography notes add Carlo De Franceschi's full bibliography and his offices — secretary of the Istrian provincial committee at Poreč 1861–76, president of the Istrian archaeological society 1866–69 — with the flat Croatian verdict «potpuno prožet talijanskim duhom Istre». **Belaj on «Crkvina i svete trokutne strukture» has nothing**: zero occurrences of the surname in 670 lines. It is a study of pre-Christian sacred landscape geometry and is not relevant to this family.

rows.what: The surname in every spelling crossed with the towns and the events — Gologorica, Gallignana, Pisino, Pazin, Fiume, Buccari, Crikvenica, Ližnjan, Fažana, Medulin, Mione, Seghetto, Omiš, Imotski, Perinuša, and the 1945 census and cadastre
rows.src: Scribd, swept from a signed-in session
rows.text: **Scribd is a library of uploaded scans, so it behaves like a bad index over good books.** Most name-plus-town queries return nothing (Gologorica, Gallignana, Pisino, Ližnjan, Medulin, Seghetto all zero) and the broad ones return noise — «Defranceschi» alone gives 517 documents, of which the top hit is a lute suite. But four real things came out of it, and one is important. **«ISTRA — Popis stanovništva 1945. / Cadastre National de l'Istrie», 664 pages, printed by Nakladni zavod Hrvatske at Zagreb in July 1946** — the ethnic cadastre the Yugoslav side took to the peace negotiations, and the source behind this archive's «twenty-five Defranceschi families left in Istria on 1 October 1945». The whole book is there. **S. Bertoša, «Puljska prezimena prema popisima krizmanika iz 1825. g.»** — Pula surnames from the confirmation lists of 1825, which bears directly on the Pula–Fažana–Ližnjan cluster this archive has just opened. **«Dalmacija — prezimena 1725»**, twice uploaded, for the Omiš and Imotski side. And **G. Radossi's historical and comparative toponymy**, 439 pages, which returns hits for both Fiume and Fažana. **What Scribd will not do is give the text.** Its reader loads page by page behind the subscription, in-document search is not offered on these files, and downloads are blocked from this browser. So the sweep's product is a shelf list rather than a reading: four titles worth having, all of them published books that should be looked for in a library or an open repository as well.

rows.text: **The Rassegna is Carlo, seen from the Slovene and Croatian side.** Fourteen mentions, all of him as a historian: «L'Istria — note storiche» (Parenzo 1879), «Sulle varie popolazioni dell'Istria» (1852), and a **«Studio critico sull'istrumento della pretesa reambulazione di confini»** that this archive's bibliography of him did not have. He appears again in the 1848 group with Michele Facchinetti and Francesco Vidulich. **«Čemu» 28 has nothing at all** — zero occurrences of the surname in eighty-three lines. It is a philosophy faculty's journal presentation and has no bearing on this family. Recorded so it is not searched again.

rows.src: The Zoppola thread — tested and cut
rows.text: **Not evidence. A Smart Match.** Four things kill it. The tree gives the same father a daughter **Lucia born 1779 and dead 1813** and a second daughter **Lucia born 19 January 1811** — a second living daughter given her sister's name, which does not happen; so these are two men. The 1813 citation names him «Giambattista De Franceschi **o Samassa**», and **Samassa is a Zoppola surname in its own right** — Samassa Rachele and Samassa Giovanni are both in Zoppola's own civil registers. A full-text sweep returns De Franceschi all across that plain: Azzano Decimo 1897, Cordenons, Pordenone 1888 and 1898, Zoppola. And **Zoppola is the Friulian plain twenty-five kilometres west of Pordenone; Carnia is sixty kilometres north, in the mountains** — so even a real link would not have been a Carnian one. The cluster is back to having no origin, which is the honest position.

rows.what: David asked whether the book could be found. It can: the full text is uploaded to both Scribd and idoc.pub, and it was read there
rows.src: Križman, «Antička svjedočanstva o Istri» (1979) — found online and read
rows.text: **Carlo De Franceschi is cited eleven times** — indexed at pages 170, 189, 192, 193, 211 and 263, with «L'Istria, note storiche» (Poreč 1879) quoted at pp. 10–11, 38ff, 45 and 67, on the topography of the Istrian war of 177 BC, the siege of Nesactium, and whether the Pontic and Adriatic Histri are one people. Križman sets him beside Kandler, Gnirs, Benussi and Zippel, and endorses his identification of Livy's **Mutila with Medulin** and Faveria with Mutvoran as the least likely to be wrong. **And it puts Gologorica in antiquity**: Gnirs's proposal that the ancient Alùon lay on the Veli potok **between Pićan and Gologorica**, where the Roman inscriptions CIL V 322, 323, 424 and 425 were found.

rows.what: Every one converted to text and tested for the surname in five spellings and for fifteen place-names, then the ones that scored were read
rows.src: Twenty-three scans from the family, read and ranked in one pass
rows.text: **Three worth a section, five worth a line, eleven with the places but not the family, and four that cannot be read at all.** The best is **«LOS FRANCESCHI, la pequeña historia de una familia»** by Napoleón Franceschi González (Caracas 2002) — the Corsican branch written from inside it, from **Ersa in Cap Corse**, first generation **Pietro Franceschi 1694–1771**, out through the French Caribbean to Venezuela, with **not one line touching Istria**. That closes the Corsica marker on the family's map. **«Atti» 39 of Rovinj** yields Camillo De Franceschi's Pula bibliography, including **«Testamenti polesani del secolo XV con alcuni cenni sulle antiche casate patrizie di Pola»** — sixteen fifteenth-century Pula wills he transcribed, which is the obvious next reading for the southern-Istrian cluster. **«Istra iz pera Nobilea»** reports the **ex libris «De Franceschi – Seghetto»** on books in the Provincial Library — the Seget house's own library — and has Camillo buying the Nobile drawings at Koper in 1934 and 1941, and Giulio drawing monuments better than Nobile did. **Four are image-only with no text layer and need OCR**: the Planckenstein almanac of Trieste 1869 (327 pages), Jelenić on the sacred art of Umag and its surroundings (135 pages), the Hrvati i Karolinzi catalogue, and «Piazza Maggiore era troppo piccola». The first two are worth the trouble; an 1869 Littoral almanac is exactly where a harbourmaster or a civic assessor is listed by name.

rows.what: A 168-megabyte image-only scan with no text layer at all, put through optical character recognition on this project's machine and then searched. 135 pages, parallel Croatian and English
rows.src: Jelenić, «Sakralno bogatstvo Umaga i okolice» — OCR'd and read
rows.text: **Four things, and one of them is a correction.** A section on **Seget**: the villa fifteen hundred metres from Umag among the vineyards on the Novigrad road, passing to the De Franceschi in **1720**, «ranije vlasništvo **Katarine Bernardo Valier**» — which gives the vendor a Christian name and **moves the Venier–Valier question to Valier**, against this site's earlier reading. The **library** confirmed from the parish's side — «vrlo bogatu knjižnicu» — matching the ex libris «De Franceschi – Seghetto» found in the Provincial Library. The **family chapel**, right of the villa entrance with its own door and a small apse outside; a wooden altar, an Assumption with St Anthony and St Catherine, an old canvas of St Lucy, a wall cupboard — **restored in the 1990s, and Mass said in it once a year on Easter Monday.** And in the parish church of Umag, a canvas of **1650**, Our Lady of the Rosary, whose painter's name is illegible but which carries **the arms of the De Franceschi of Umag — nineteen years before the flight from Candia.** Either the arms were added later by a donor family, or the name was at Umag before 1669. Not resolved, and not guessed at.

rows.what: 327 pages of city directory, scanned at 122 megabytes with no text layer; converted on this project's machine and searched for the surname in every spelling
rows.src: «Guida schematica di Trieste» 1869 — OCR'd and read
rows.text: **Four occurrences in three hundred and twenty-seven pages, and two of them are people.** «**Defranceschi Corrado, controllore in pens., V. Caserma 12**» — a retired controller of the imperial financial service, listed among the possidenti e privati. And «**Gleyre Costante (Enrico de Franceschi), in manifatture e pece, V. S. Spiridione 7**» — a merchant house in textiles and pitch, with Enrico de Franceschi named as the man behind it. The other two are Franceschinelli and Defrancesco, different formations of the same root, recorded so the next search does not stop at them. Nothing joins either man to a line on this site; what the book proves is that two households of the name were living and trading in Trieste in 1869, twenty years before Camillo De Franceschi settled there. The directories for other years would say whether they stayed.

rows.what: «Acquisitions» has sat on this project's research log as a wish list for months. DAPA publishes a current price list; it was read, and most of what was wanted turns out to be in print and cheap
rows.src: The Pazin archive's own price list — the acquisitions queue, priced
rows.text: **Seven titles, about a hundred and fifty-four euro, and the first three would close three questions this site currently prints as open.** **Jelinčić's «Knjiga ređenja u Pićnu (Prothocollum) 1632–1783», €19.91** — a hundred and fifty years of Pedena ordinations, and an ordination entry names the ordinand's father. This archive has four priests of the name it cannot place. **Orbanić's edition of de Buset's spiritual visitation of 1788, €13.27**, 477 pages, ISBN 978-953-7640-30-9, published in the Vatican and covering Gologorica and Gallignana parish by parish in the last year of the diocese of Pićan. **Doblanović Šuran and Mogorović Crljenko, «Matična knjiga krštenih župe Umag 1483–1643», €26.54** — which is the direct test of the 1650 painting in Umag that carries the family arms nineteen years before the family is supposed to have arrived. Then **Joksimović's edition of Valier's 1580 apostolic visitation of the diocese of Pula, €60**, aimed straight at the unplaced southern-Istrian cluster; the **1571 urbarium of the County of Pazin, €10**; Slukan Altić's «Katastar Istre», €9.29; and DAPA's own beginner's guide to genealogy in its holdings, €15. Two wanted volumes are sold out. Both the translator and the editor of the 1788 visitation — **Jakov Jelinčić and Elvis Orbanić** — are already on this project's list of people to write to, and both work at Pazin.

rows.text: **Nine issues, named and dated — and the reader is behind a bot check.** The search itself runs: *Gazzetta di Zara*, 4 August 1840 (3 hits in the text); *Agramer Zeitung*, 27 December 1845 and 6 July 1898; *Vereinigte Laibacher Zeitung*, 8 June 1876, and *Laibacher Tagblatt*, 23 June 1876 — the same story from two papers a fortnight apart; *Il giovine Pensiero* of Pula, 21 December 1894 and 1 August 1896; the *Pharmaceutischer Almanach* of 1904 (4 hits); and the *Allgemeine Sport-Zeitung* of 1886. **The page viewer at data.onb.ac.at is behind a Cloudflare check, and this archive does not answer those.** The nine citations are exact and any reader can open them; what cannot be done from here is read them. The Zadar paper of 1840 is the one to open first.

rows.what: A queued item finally worked: the site's page of his selected works
rows.src: IstriaNet — Camillo De Franceschi's collected bibliography
rows.text: **Forty-five entries between 1898 and 1964, with volumes and pages**, compiled from the Italian librarians' biographical database and the Trieste civic library catalogue. Three land on questions open on this site today. **«Testamenti polesani del secolo XV, con alcuni cenni sulle antiche casate patrizie di Pola», AMSI 42 (1930), pp. 167–219** — now properly cited, and aimed straight at the unplaced Pula cluster. **«La popolazione di Pola nel secolo XV e nei seguenti», Archeografo Triestino ser. 3 vol. 3 (1906), pp. 221–315** — the same question from the other side, ninety-four pages of it. And **«Quando e da chi sia stato ideato l'apocrifo istrumento di confinazione della Contea di Pisino con la data del 1325», Archivio Veneto ser. 5, 30/31 (1942)** — in which Camillo, of Gologorica, argues that the Istrian Boundary Settlement is a forgery, a document whose Glagolitic version was written by the parish priest of Gologorica. Also «I Castelli della Val d'Arsa» (1900), with unpublished documents and genealogical trees, and «Ricordi di biblioteca» (1959), seventy-four pages by the man who bought the Nobile drawings and shelved the Seget library.

rows.text: **Nothing, and it is not even the right century.** One hundred and thirty-one pages converted; a single occurrence of the name, and it is **Lydia Franceschi**, in a report of an Italian workers' and students' meeting of the late 1970s. The book is about the Bologna student movement. No Istrian place-name in it worth the count. Recorded so it is never opened for this purpose again.

rows.text: **One occurrence of the surname, and it is at Omiš, not Bakar.** A state-property auction notice of the I.R. Pretura d'Almissa, 6 July 1840, lists a vineyard at Strane in Vrisovec «tenuto a colonia al quarto da **D. Nicolò Defranceschi**», fiscal value fl. 8 k. 20. **«Buccari» appears in a wholly separate notice pages away** — so ANNO's pairing is whole-issue co-occurrence, not a Defranceschi at Bakar, and the Bakar lead is weaker than it looked. Published on the Omiš line. PDF fetched by David; the bot check was not answered.

rows.what: Two hundred pages of the fourth image-only scan converted and searched
rows.src: «Hrvati i Karolinzi» — the 2000 exhibition catalogue, OCR'd
rows.text: **No person of the name, and none expected** — the catalogue is about the ninth century. But the surname is in it three times, and every one of them is **Camillo De Franceschi in the bibliography**, cited for his 1932 and 1933 work on the early-medieval church sculpture of Pula and Sv. Ivan od Nimfeja, alongside Gnirs, Marušić, Šonje and Rapanić. Sixty-seven years after he published, the standard national catalogue of Croatia's Carolingian-period art still cites him by name. Recorded as a nil return for people and a footnote for Camillo.

rows.what: The queued migration paper, read in full — from the publisher's open PDF, not from academia.edu
rows.src: Darovec, «Migration to Istria and the North Adriatic in the Modern Age» (2021)
rows.text: **No occurrence of the surname, and the best contextual source this archive has found.** It puts both of our Istrian arrivals inside documented movements: the *Carni* as one of the named peoples of Istria in Petronio's list of 1681, settling exactly at **Pazin, Pićan, Gradišće, Žminj and Tinjan**; the Slavicisation of immigrant Friulian surnames (*Furlanich*, *Callegarich*), which is the mechanism behind **Defrančeski**; and **twelve Venetian attempts between 1530 and 1669** to settle Greeks from Crete and the Morea in Istria, the survivors absorbed into the Italian-speaking towns. Published on the Lines page. Note for method: academia.edu is behind a bot check this archive will not answer, and the paper was open on the publisher's own site all along.

rows.what: «Rotilio» as a given name across the Argentine record; the surname in Argentina 1900–1910; and the whole United States index
rows.src: Rotilio Defranceschi, in Argentina and in America
rows.text: **Nothing, and the lore loses its one prop.** A dozen Argentine Rotilios — Voltolini, Cichini, Moreira, Jurado, Ballesteros — and not one of the surname; a dozen Argentine Defranceschi, all of them an Italian-mainland stock with Piergiacomi and Rosso in-laws, and not one Rotilio. Meanwhile the album's detail that «he married Albina Chinkopan» turns out to be **his sister's marriage**: Albina De Franceschi, born 14 April 1900, married Frank Chinkopan of the same village and died at Brooklyn in 1945. Published on the Eleven.

rows.what: United States naturalizations, censuses, death certificates and the Numident, searched for every child of Antonio the mason
rows.src: The Eleven of Gračišće, against the American record
rows.text: **Five of the eleven documented in New York, four of them in Brooklyn.** The proof is a misspelling: Albina's New York death certificate of 27 April 1945 names her mother **«Maria Walhart»** and Bruno's naturalization names her **«Mary Walhal»** — both of them the **Volhardt** the Gračišće priest wrote in 1925. Also corrects this archive: Antonio «Tony», whom the album put in Italy, naturalised at Brooklyn in 1922 and 1929.

rows.what: Every spelling of the surname searched across the whole of Germany, after the archive realised it had been searching the wrong Monheim
rows.src: Monheim — the German telephone directory, nationally
rows.text: **One private listing in the entire country**, spelt «Defranceski» exactly as this family spells it, at **Langenfeld (Rheinland) — five kilometres from Monheim am Rhein, in the same district**. The only «Defranceschi» in Germany is a company at Mannheim, the German arm of an Italian winery-equipment firm. This archive had been reading the map pin's coordinates literally and searching **Bavaria**; there are two Monheims and it was looking at the wrong one. Living people, so no one is named. Published on the Ližnjan page as a correction.

rows.what: The Carnia–Istria emigration study hosted openly by the Amici dell'Orologeria Pesarina, searched for every occurrence of the surname
rows.src: Brhan, «Stare cum loco et foco» — the fourth paper, read in full
rows.text: **Twenty-two occurrences, and one of them closes a gap this archive has flagged as open on four pages.** Brhan prints the Catasto franceschino of 1820 for Moncalvo: **six De Franceschi proprietor households — Maria, Giuseppe, «Giobatta (di Gallignana)», Leonardo and Antonio** — «the most influential family» in a district of ten Croatian villages. A Giobatta *of Gallignana* holding at Moncalvo is the first object that puts the two villages together. Also new: a **Stanzia De Franceschi at Sanvincenti**, lost by 1820; Defranceschi among the Carnian families in the Barban contrade; and, after Bertoša 1985, that the Moncalvo family came from **Agrons** with gismanial feudal rights and that the **Umag family is of «un'origine completamente diversa»**. Academia.edu hosts it too, behind a bot check; the Carnian association's own site does not.

rows.what: The published register of fonds of the State Archive in Rijeka, for both De Franceschi fonds
rows.src: HR-DARI-254 — the family's own archive, finding aid read in full
rows.text: **The 1610 problem is closed.** The fond's earliest item is the **Glagolitic income book of the parish church at Hum, 1610–1685** — the only Croatian-language item in it, and part of the family's *collection*, not its papers. The collector was «most probably Carlo De Franceschi». The family's own earliest paper is **1703**. Also recovered: an eighteenth-century business of **money-lending and buying up debts** reaching Kastav, Mošćenice, Labin and Carniola; and the fact that **until 1990 this fond was physically merged with the Šeget family's fond «through ignorance of the family's history»** — the same confusion this site argues against, made by the archive that holds both.

rows.what: The standard dictionary of Venetian toponymy, downloaded whole and searched for the surname
rows.src: Tassini, «Curiosità veneziane» (1872) — the Venetian street-name authority
rows.text: **The street is real and the entry is a windfall.** «FRANCESCHI (Rio terrà dei) a' SS. Apostoli» — and before the canal was filled in it was crossed by **a Ponte dei Franceschi**. Named for the *cittadini* family whose arms were **a lion rampant, motto «Sero sapimus»**, and specifically for the houses of **Benda Franceschi (redecima of 1514)** and her nephew and heir **Andrea, Grand Chancellor**, who declared a *casa da statio* there in 1537. Four new facts about Andrea, three further Venetian vignettes, and one earlier dismissal reopened.

rows.what: Croatian sources, the maritime-heritage register and the Rijeka chronologies
rows.text: **There is no bridge. There is a pier — «De Franceschijev gat», the former Mol Zichy**, in the main harbour: 150 m east, 134 m west, 80 m south. The first iron-and-concrete building in the port went up on it in 1882, and the **first electric light in Rijeka was lit on it**, by Zipernowsky, with lamps borrowed from the Torpedo Factory. **Who the De Franceschi is, no source says**; the city archive would settle it.

rows.what: The Status Animarum page re-read at full magnification, and every index searched in every spelling of both names
rows.text: **Alive at home and unmarried in about 1848, and then nothing at all.** The house 5 page gives him all four sacramental ticks and **leaves both the marriage and the death column empty** — as it does for all four sons. The indexes have no Raymundus, Raimondo, Rajmund or Raymond of this surname anywhere on earth, in any century. The eldest son of the house vanishes and the second son inherits, which is why this archive's whole spine runs through Antonio. Three bounded things would break it: the Gallignana death register 1848–1880, the marriage register for the same years, and the Austrian conscription lists for the County of Pazin.

rows.what: The full paper, fetched from an open repository after the Croatian journal host went behind a bot check
rows.text: Confirms and sharpens what this archive already quoted. The Carnian surnames — De Franceschi, Crosila, Bergamo, Moro, Fiorencis — are in the 1734 Status animarum **only inside the castello of Svetvinčenat, not in the villages around it**, and the Carnians «were mainly in trade», working as **prekupci i preprodavači — buyers-up and resellers**. The same economic type the Rijeka finding aid describes for the Gologorica house: money-lending and buying up debts.

rows.what: Four queued Croatian journal and thesis PDFs
rows.text: **Both are now behind bot checks that this archive will not answer.** hrcak.srce.hr returns «Confirm you're not a robot», and so does the Dabar repository network that carries the Pula and Koper university theses. This archive has used hrcak successfully before, so this is a change rather than a rule. Where a paper exists elsewhere — a university's own site, CORE, an author's page — it can still be read; the Doblanović paper above was got that way. Recorded so the same doors are not knocked on twice.

rows.what: An open-access article on Venetian-organised settlement in Istria
rows.src: Pomara, «An Attempted Albanian Settlement in Istria (1610–1612)», Diasporas 43 (2025)
rows.text: **No person of the name.** Carlo De Franceschi is cited as an authority — on the depopulation of Istria and on Poreč falling to some three hundred souls by 1601 — which is one more instance of the historian still being quoted, this time in 2025. Nothing for the family.

rows.src: Pomorski i povijesni muzej Hrvatskog primorja, Rijeka

rows.what: A search for the Šeget fond's finding aid turned this up instead
rows.text: **The family's library is not lost. It is in Zagreb, and it has been catalogued.** 2,396 items, 1503–1945, taken out of the house at Gologorica in 1948–49, boxed, and left unprocessed in the National and University Library's store for sixty years — not in the card catalogue, not in the electronic one, «nobody could know of its existence». Processing began 2009 and finished in 2021. It holds an Aldine of 1503, the signatures of five generations, letters of D'Annunzio, poems of Giuseppina Martinuzzi, and the very Metastasio, Petrarch, Tasso and Ariosto that Carlo says he found on the family shelves as a schoolboy. Published on the Library page.

rows.what: 386 given names × four spellings of the surname, then a person-panel fetch for every hit
rows.src: MyHeritage, tree 4 — the whole surname re-harvested
rows.text: **573 individuals of the name in the live tree** — a hundred and fourteen more than the harvest of a year ago, which ran on a shorter name list. Merged into the roster, they take it from 577 people to **1,021**, of whom **572 now carry a FamilySearch record link and 513 a link into the tree**. They also open two clusters this archive had barely registered: **forty-four in Trentino and South Tyrol** — Telve, Strigno, Fiera di Primiero, Laives, Cles — and the **Corsican family at Tomino and Mandolacce**, which the Lines page already draws as its own lane. The earliest are three at Pula born 1669, 1671 and 1674.

rows.what: The three earliest people in the roster, traced from index entry to image ark to film to catalogue
rows.text: **A method, and a correction.** FamilySearch's Croatian index often gives no parish at all — just «Croazia, Austria». But every persona carries the ark of the image it was read from, and the digital-archive service turns that ark into a **DGS film number**, which the catalogue names. The three earliest — born 1669, 1671 and 1674 — resolve to **DGS 005497884 = «Matična knjiga 1568–1917», Župa Svetvinčenat**. Which means the entries this archive has published for a year as «**Pula 1667**», the opening of the whole southern-Istrian line, are **Svetvinčenat entries**. The same film gives a continuous De Franceschi presence there from **1657 to 1737** under twelve different fathers. This is now standard practice for any «Croazia, Austria» row.

rows.what: 954 indexed records of the surname traced from index entry to image ark to DGS film to catalogue
rows.src: The whole Croatian index, resolved film by film
rows.text: **Ninety-three parishes.** This archive had eighteen. The Croatian index mostly gives no parish — «Croazia, Austria» — but every persona carries the ark of the image it was read from, and that resolves to a film, and the film is named. Done for all 954 records it draws the map: **Omiš 145 from 1634, Rijeka 105 from 1626, Ližnjan 100 from 1794, Svetvinčenat 85 from 1666, Pula 63 from 1659**, and Bakar exactly five, 1772–1819, which is the household this archive had already reconstructed from another direction. New and unsuspected: **Vižinada 53**, Draguč 25, **Rovinj 23 from 1619** — the earliest date on the map — **Dubrovnik 38** across two parishes, and Bednja and Pregrada in the Zagorje from 1706 and 1674. Published as a chart on the Every Town page.

rows.what: Every record id in the film map joined back onto the 1,021 people
rows.src: The roster, attributed parish by parish
rows.text: **367 of the 1,021 now carry the name of the parish register they were actually found in**, across 27 parishes — recovered from records the index labelled only «Croazia, Austria». The «no place» bucket falls from 386 people to 185, and «not placed» rises from 150 to 323, which is the honest direction: naming the parish usually tells you the family is one this archive has not attached to a line. Filterable on the People page as «Parish known».

rows.what: Images 397, 398 and 442 opened tile by tile and read line by line
rows.src: Svetvinčenat parish register, DGS 005497884 — read, not searched
rows.text: **Three unindexed occurrences on the first three openings.** «M.ro Nadal de Franceschi» stands godfather on 20 May 1666, five months before his own daughter is baptised; «il Sig.r Ant.o di Franceschi» stands godfather on 9 February 1674. Godparent roles are never indexed, which is the whole reason to open the page. The baptisms of Colotta (24 Oct 1666) and Fioretta (22 Nov 1666) are confirmed word for word, both fathers styled **M.ro**. And the company is the argument: the godparents across these openings are **Spinoti, Fiorenza, Felicer, Fabri** — the Canale di Gorto set, standing at each other's fonts in a Croatian village in 1666. By 1674 Anto is **Sig.r** and his son's compare is a **Count Luciani**: the same household, eight years, artisan to gentleman.

rows.what: The godfather at Mattio de Franceschi's baptism, traced through the index and the films
rows.text: **He is of the Albona house.** The surname enlarges cleanly to **Lucciani**; the place after «da» will not settle between D and R. The index carries a Luciani family baptising at exactly these dates — Bartolomio Zuane on 12 November 1674, and five more between 1682 and 1693 — and every one of them resolves to the parish register of **Labin (Albona)**, DGS 005494791–2. Which closes a circle: Carlo De Franceschi names «cav. Tomaso Luciani … di Albona» among his sources in 1879, Luciani's **ex libris** is in the family library now at Zagreb, and Hauptmann found **letters of Tomaso Luciani** in the wrecked house at Gologorica in 1945. Two hundred years, one surname, one town — pairing stated, descent not claimed.

rows.what: Carlo De Franceschi's «L'Istria: note storiche» (1879) downloaded whole and searched
rows.src: Count Damian de Franceschis (Gallignana, 1720) — searched again
rows.text: **Not there.** The full text of Carlo's own history of Istria contains no Damiano de Franceschi and no count of the surname — nine occurrences of «Franceschi» in the whole book, none of them him. So the only man ever recorded as **Comes Damianus de Franceschis** is still known from exactly one line of one baptism register, and the family's own historian, writing a hundred and sixty years later about his own county, had never heard of him.

rows.src: Svetvinčenat film, seven openings read band by band
rows.text: **Eight occurrences the index does not have, all godparent roles**, plus four baptisms confirmed word for word. The best line is «Comp.ri furono **M.ro Ant.o di Franceschi di Piero**» (25 Oct 1667) — a patronymic, which gives Anto a father and pushes the family a generation behind the twelve the index knows. Also: Mattia of 1669 is «fig.a… nata», **a daughter**, not the son the name suggested; Anto stands godfather twice in eight days in October 1669; and the honorifics turn out **not** to be a clean ladder — M.ro, S.r and no style at all all appear in 1669–71, which corrects a tidier claim published here earlier. Carnian company in the same pages: **Spinotti, Fiorencis, Felice, Fabris, Festa**. Twelve openings of this film still to read.

rows.what: A first pass at David's request that our people have faces, as his old site's did
rows.src: Wikimedia Commons — portraits for the people pages
rows.text: **Seven images found, licensed, captioned and wired in** — and one of them is a discovery in its own right. Searching for Domenico de' Franceschi the printer turned up the title page of **Palladio's «I quattro libri dell'architettura», Venice 1570, «Appresso Dominico de' Franceschi»** — the most influential architectural book ever printed, and this archive's entry for him had never mentioned it. Also: a portrait of **Carlo De Franceschi** (PD, before 1893); Domenico's own woodcut of **Charles V storming La Goletta** from the Statens Museum for Kunst; the **Vayron lithograph of Franceschi-Delonne** and Philippoteaux's painting of his capture in 1809; the **Dien engraving after Riesener of Jean-Marie-Antoine Defrance, 1820** — which also supplies his death year, 1835, that this archive lacked; and the National Gallery of Art's *After Titian* portrait of **Andrea de' Franceschi** (CC0). Built by a new tool, `tools/commons.py`, which keeps every image's Commons page, licence, author and date.

rows.src: Svetvinčenat, DGS 005497884 — nineteen openings, the indexed run complete
rows.text: **Twenty occurrences the index does not have**, sixteen of them godparent roles. Eleven baptisms verbatim; one filiation («Ant.o di Franceschi **di Piero**»); one death dated (Batta, before July 1688); three people added; one sex corrected (Mattia 1669 is a daughter); **one duplicate found in the register itself** — a boy called Piero baptised twice, 6 and 15 October 1707, to a father written Nardo once and Lunardo once and a mother Eufemia both times, with **the same two godparents in both entries**; one within-family godparent link; and **M.ro Mattio Lupieri** standing for a De Franceschi child in 1707. It also overturned this archive's own reading of opening 578 as empty — it is not. **What the film did not give is an origin** — not one entry says where these people came from. And 576 of its 595 images, including all the marriages and deaths, are still unread.

rows.what: A register's own error, kept as it stands
rows.text:
**This archive said** «Il Signor Carlo De Franceschi … celibe, **d'anni 40**», 1 March 1852.

**What is true** He was **forty-two**, born 16 October 1809.

**How it happened** Not this archive's mistake but the register's, and it is transcribed as written rather than silently improved. Ages in these books are what somebody said in the room — and in this room the man being asked was too ill to stand up.

rows.what: Names that are not this name
rows.text:
**This archive said** Nothing — these were caught before publication and are recorded so they are not found again.

**What is true** **Franceschich** of Buzet is a Slavic patronymic, not Franceschi. **Francin** is its own Vodnjan family — although Pietro De Franceschi's first wife was a Francin, so in that parish the two are a household deep in each other. **Pietro Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel** is not a De Franceschi.

**How it happened** Read by eye rather than matched by string. This is the whole argument for reading a register instead of querying one.
